articles.title: The 2-drop dish soap trick that stops window condensation (and black mold) in its tracks
articles.content: Fighting window condensation shouldn’t mean continually running one of the best dehumidifiers or wiping down your glass every morning, the best solution I’ve found so far is already sitting by your kitchen sink. Left unchecked, condensation on cold glass quickly turns into soaked sills, warped trim, and stubborn black mold . After years of waking up to dripping windows, I switched to a quick, streak-free habit that breaks water’s surface tension before droplets can even form. Why a drop of dish soap keeps windows clear Condensation turns visible and destructive when water molecules cling to cold glass in dense droplets, creating a cloudy film that eventually pools on your window trim. Because dish soap is a surfactant, applying a trace amount directly to dry glass with a microfiber cloth disrupts that surface tension. (Image credit: Shutterstock) Moisture still settles on the cold pane overnight but it can no longer form droplets, flattening instead into an invisible layer that keeps the glass clear and prevents heavy beading. While this quick trick won't stop excess room humidity from needing proper ventilation, it is an easy way to stop your windows from fogging up every morning. How to apply dish soap without leaving streaks Using too much soap will leave a cloudy smear across your view, so a light touch is key. First things first, get your windows clean . Clear away any dust, dirt, or existing morning moisture with a dry cloth so you are working on a clean, dry pane. (Image credit: Shutterstock) Apply the dish soap directly onto a dry microfiber cloth rather than straight onto the window. Then simply rub the cloth firmly across the pane in circular motions until every trace of soap disappears and the glass looks completely streak-free. 3 quick rules to keep in mind Avoid rubbing neat dish soap onto the rubber gaskets around your window frame , as concentrated detergents can dry out and degrade rubber over time. Reapply every week or two . Moisture gradually wears away the invisible barrier, so simply buff on a fresh drop whenever droplets start returning. Because indoor humidity still has to go somewhere, excess moisture can settle on cold walls if a room stays sealed. Pair this trick with opening your windows for 10 minutes each morning , often called " house burping ", or using a dehumidifier when drying clothes indoors. articles.title: Motorola confirms some Signature 27 buyers will get a much smaller battery
articles.content: TL;DR Motorola has confirmed to Android Authority that Germany is getting the Signature 27 with a different battery configuration. The German variant packs a 5,500mAh battery instead of the 7,000mAh unit available in other markets. Motorola attributes the downgrade to local lithium battery regulations affecting transportation and logistics. A massive 7,000mAh battery is one of the biggest selling points of the Motorola Signature 27 , a phone that packs just about everything you’d expect from a modern Android flagship. But as we discovered last week, not everyone buying Motorola’s latest premium smartphone will get to enjoy that headline-grabbing battery capacity . We now know where and why. In a statement to Android Authority , a Motorola spokesperson confirmed that the company is using a different battery configuration for the German market due to local regulatory requirements.

articles.title: I used Google's new Gemini 4 Hydrogen to find out where my paycheck goes — and it only took one prompt
articles.content: Google's latest AI model might be one of its most useful yet, especially if you've ever wished you could create your own app without knowing how to code. The model is designed to be faster and more efficient at everyday tasks, including coding, research, analyzing documents and building interactive websites. Unlike Gemini 4 Carbon , which focuses on more demanding reasoning tasks, Hydrogen prioritizes getting things done quickly without sacrificing too much intelligence. But what caught my attention was Google's claim that Hydrogen can build more functional, feature-complete websites in fewer prompts. I immediately thought about our family budget. Between groceries, recurring bills, subscriptions and the everyday purchases that add up faster than expected, I wanted something that would show where our money was going without requiring me to build a complicated spreadsheet. Better yet, I wanted something I could share with my husband so we could look at the numbers together. Note : for this experiment, these numbers are arbitrary. Which reminds me, be sure your app is secure before sharing financial information. The Gemini Hydrogen prompt to try (Image credit: Future) Here's the exact prompt I used to create a budget for my family: Build me a fully functional, interactive website that helps me figure out where my money goes every month. I want to enter my monthly income, recurring bills, groceries, subscriptions and miscellaneous expenses. The website should automatically calculate how much money I have left, show an interactive breakdown of my spending, identify my three biggest opportunities to save money and let me simulate what happens if I cancel subscriptions or reduce spending. Make it beautiful, modern, mobile-friendly and simple enough for someone who doesn't understand budgeting. Use realistic sample data so I can test it immediately. Make every button, slider and calculation functional, not just decorative. Do not ask follow-up questions. Make reasonable design decisions yourself and build the complete experience. Before finishing, check the calculations, test the interactions and correct any problems you find. Tell me if anything could not be verified. Why this prompt works so well with Hydrogen (Image credit: Shutterstock) What makes this prompt interesting is that there are several things happening at once. Gemini needs to create the website, build the calculations, organize the information in a way that makes sense and connect everything so the numbers update when you change your spending. The key is the interactivity of the site. For example, canceling a $15 subscription should immediately increase the amount of money you have left by $15. Reducing your grocery budget should change your spending breakdown, and the savings recommendations should reflect the expenses you've entered. It's exactly the kind of interactive web development that Google says Hydrogen is particularly good at. And best of all, you don't have to be "coder" to make it work for you. The prompt also gives Gemini some creative freedom. You can certainly tell the model what colors you want, but I kept the prompt short for the sake of function. I didn't specify colors, layouts or exactly where every button should go because I just wanted to see my money/budget all in one place. You can do that, but you don't have to because the model make those design decisions on its own so you can focus on other things. How to try it yourself (Image credit: Future) Head to Gemini and select Gemini 4 Hydrogen from the model options. It was the default for me, but if not, just select it from the model picker. It's free for everyone. If you don't see it, try logging out and refreshing. Google says Hydrogen is rolling out to users globally, although free accounts may access it through automatic model selection rather than a dedicated model choice. articles.title: 5 lesser-known Apple Watch features I swear by — from personal safety tools to a smarter way to wake up
articles.content: The best Apple Watches are capable of some pretty remarkable things, like sending for help if you take a nasty fall, predicting your daily readiness, and logging physical fitness. But with so much capability, some of the most useful Apple Watch tools and apps inevitably fly under the radar. That's where I come in. I'm Dan, and I lead TG's smartwatch review coverage. I'm also an avid Apple Watch wearer with strong opinions and a knack for tinkering with settings. With that in mind, here are five favorite lesser-known Apple Watch features that I absolutely swear by. Some were added via the recent watchOS 27 release, while others are old standbys. Note: This list expands my previously published 7 hidden Apple Watch features I swear by round-up from earlier in the year. 1. Calculator tip button to handle checks like a pro (Image credit: Dan Bracaglia/Tom's Guide) Dividing up a check between friends can be a tedious task, especially if you and your pals aren't math whizzes. If only there were a super-simple way to calculate a tip and split a check without breaking a sweat. There is! Your Apple Watch's boring old Calculator app features a built-in tip button. Simply enter the total amount of the check and tap "Tip." This brings up a screen where you can enter your desired tip percentage and the number of individuals paying for an instant calculation. And just like that, you'll never fumble a check again. 2. Single-tap gesture to open for favorite widgets (Image credit: Future) Apple first introduced the double-tap gesture control for Apple Watch back in 2023. Simply tap your index finger and thumb together twice on your watch-wearing wrist to execute actions like answering a call, closing an app, stopping a timer, or pausing a song. In 2026, Apple added a single-tap gesture that works in exactly the same way, minus the second tap. To set it up, head to Settings > Gestures. Super-useful, I have my double-tap programmed to open the Smart Stack, while the single-tap opens my most recent/active widget, all without interacting with the screen or buttons. 3. Check in with friends for safety (Image credit: Dan Bracaglia/Tom's Guide) When it comes to on-wrist safety, I'd argue that Apple and Google lead the pack, and one of my favorite Apple Watch personal safety features, Check In, often gets overlooked. Check In is a reliable and simple way to keep friends and/or loved ones looped into your location at critical times. For example, I can set a Check In when I leave my apartment that automatically alerts my partner when I arrive at my set destination. Or, if you're an avid runner, you can use the feature to automatically keep those you trust informed of when you both depart and arrive safely back home. Here's a deeper dive into how to use one of Apple's best safety features . 4. Compass backtrack to find your way (Image credit: Future) While on the subject of safety, I'd be remiss not to mention Apple's equally valuable Backtrack safety feature, which is particularly useful when exploring new places, if for nothing else, peace of mind. Backtrack works like a digital breadcrumb trail, allowing you to retrace your steps back to your starting location via turn-by-turn directions in the event you get lost. Best of all, it works both in urban environments and out in nature. Here's more on how to set up and use Apple's Backtrack tool . 5. Silent/vibration alarm for a better, brighter morning (Image credit: Dan Bracaglia/Tom's Guide) Last but not least, and perhaps the easiest to miss, we have Apple's silent, vibration-based alarm clock. This is by no means a new feature, but it's one I adore and use daily. As a U.S. West Coast-based writer with colleagues primarily in New York and London, my days tend to start quite early. Rather than risking waking my sleep partner or puppy, I schedule my alarm and set my Apple Watch 12 to silent. This switches the wake-up alert from an audible one to a vibration-based one, which I also find to be a gentler way…

articles.title: Japan's Fugaku supercomputer has decidedly un-super security
articles.content: The RIKEN Center for Computational Science, the home of the Fugaku supercomputer, has revealed unauthorized attempts to access the machine after a data leak. According to a statement issued by RIKEN yesterday, between November 10 and 13 an unknown entity attacked a web dashboard that displays operational status data for Fugaku. It sounds like whatever the attackers did to that dashboard allowed them to move across the RIKEN network, because they were able to reach several servers that store data belonging to authorized users, and install malware. The servers stored users’ names and email addresses, plus credentials used to access supercomputers and services not operated by RIKEN. The attacker has tried to use those credentials. RIKEN is working with the organizations that host those other supercomputers to investigate whether the attackers succeeded. The research outfit doesn’t know how the attack happened and can’t say with certainty what information attackers were able to access and/or steal, beyond saying that 4,222 registered users of Fugaku are at risk, along with 375 registered users of its smaller Rikyu supercomputer. RIKEN does know that on November 13, someone attempted to log onto Fugaku. RIKEN quickly took the machine offline. Fugaku comprises 158,976 nodes, each packing a 48-core processor and 32GiB of available RAM, for a total of 7,630,848 cores and over five petabytes of memory. Those specs saw Fugaku lead the Top 500 lists of Earth’s mightiest supercomputers for two years between 2020 and 2022. It ranks ninth on the update of the list released on Tuesday. RIKEN’s other super, Rikyu, operates 288,000 cores. If attackers managed to run a workload on either machine, they could do a lot of damage. The intrusion has already had serious consequences because Fugaku is currently offline. As the machine is used for scientific research, and RIKEN schedules use of the machine, the outage will disrupt researchers who were waiting for their turn to use the supercomputer. At the time of writing, RIKEN has found no evidence that users’ research data has leaked but isn’t yet sure what info did make it out of the building and whether it contains any data describing third parties. The research org has promised to conduct a detailed investigation into the incident, which is the latest in a long string of significant cyberattacks that have struck Japanese clouds , telcos , retailers and government agencies, leading Tokyo to release emergency funds in the hope that extra money can quickly shore up the nation’s cyber-defenses. ®

articles.title: I drove the $95K 2027 Audi S6 Sportback e-tron for a week — 543 horsepower, an AR head-up display, and a subscription-free dashcam make this a standout EV despite one major quirk
articles.content: When I got into the driver's seat of the Audi A6 Sportback e-tron last year, my expectations weren’t all that high. But it ended up impressing me so much that it quickly became one of the best electric cars I’ve tested. With the 2027 Audi S6 Sportback e-tron , it’s pretty evident that Audi has dialed up the aggression and sportier flair. While there are similarities between the two, the S6 Sportback e-tron differentiates itself with standard dual-motor quattro all-wheel drive, sport-tuned adaptive air suspension, and up to 543 horsepower. Quite simply, it’s a mid-size luxury sedan that trades some range for extra muscle. I tested the 2027 Audi S6 Sportback e-tron Prestige for a week, which carries a $94,490 as-tested price — putting it squarely in the crosshairs of similar models I’ve tested, like the BMW i5 and Lucid Air Touring . articles.title: HBO releases first clip from its new ‘Harry Potter’ TV show — the internet immediately calls it ‘insulting,’ ‘lifeless’ and ‘Temu Harry Potter’
articles.content: HBO Max has released a first look at its upcoming ‘Harry Potter’ TV show, and it’s fair to say the online reaction has been mixed . And by mixed, I mean mostly extremely negative. The 90-second clip is presumably from an early episode (I would guess episode 2). It offers a first look at Hogwarts’ start-of-term feast, alongside a brief conversation between headmaster Albus Dumbledore (John Lithgow) and professor of Transfiguration Minerva McGonagall (Janet McTeer). The show, which will be called “Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone” for its first season (no, Sorcerer’s Stone this time), will adapt J.K. Rowling’s 1997 book of the same name across a reported eight episodes. Dominic McLaughlin will play the boy wizard, with Alastair Stout and Arabella Stanton playing his schoolmates Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger, respectively. The first episode is due to premiere on HBO in the U.S. and HBO Max internationally on December 25, and it’s already been earmarked as one of the most anticipated (and most expensive) television projects in history. I suspect HBO was hoping this clip would be well-received… The internet isn’t holding back with its reaction (Image credit: HBO) HBO’s “Harry Potter” has faced backlash since its initial announcement in 2023. The necessity of adapting Rowling’s best-selling books a second time has been questioned, as the movie versions, released between 2001 and 2011, remain extremely popular to this day. And are seasonal staples for many. Also, you can’t talk about Harry Potter in the current climate without acknowledging the controversy surrounding its creator, J.K. Rowling. Rowling has become an extremely divisive public figure due to her outspoken views, particularly in relation to the transgender community, which makes anything related to the Harry Potter brand controversial. One look at my feeds, and the initial reactions to this short teaser clip haven’t exactly been magical. Over on X, the clip has been labeled “lifeless in all aspects,” and comparisons to the same scene in the 2001 movie starring Daniel Radcliffe, which is noticeably more colorful, have done few favors. This new Harry Potter looks so lifeless man in all aspects. https://t.co/NeLhmHNTpW November 15, 2026 One post from X user Matt del Rio, which has amassed more than 35,000 likes as of writing, reads, “As a millennial who spent hours upon hours reading Harry Potter growing up, I’m insulted by this,” suggesting that even viewers who haven’t turned their back on the series in the wake of Rowling’s incendiary comments are unimpressed with HBO’s first look. As a millennial who spent hours upon hours reading Harry Potter growing up, I’m insulted by this November 15, 2026 And as far as cutting remarks go, one X account states, “It’s actually so funny they spent millions of dollars to make Temu Harry Potter.” Ouch! Probably not the reaction HBO would be hoping for, considering the show reportedly cost roughly $25 million per episode to produce. it’s actually so funny they spent millions of dollars to make Temu Harry Potter November 15, 2026 Does HBO’s Harry Potter show the dangers of nostalgia? As one of the biggest Harry Potter fans on staff at Tom’s Guide — a label that comes with an uncomfortable degree of shame these days — my feelings on this first clip are decidedly more muted. Overall, I think, judging solely on this new 90-second clip, the show looks generally fine. The problem is that for millions of us, myself included, we literally grew up on the Potter movies, so there is an inherent disconnect when watching a new production of “The Philosopher’s Stone.” It’s hard to see anybody as Harry Potter but a young Daniel Radcliffe. Getting past the nostalgic fondness so many have for the movies will be tough. (Image credit: Warner Bros.) I do agree with the criticism of the lack of color, but this seems to be a trend across modern TV shows and movies. The art of color grading seems to be a dying one. Not to mention the lack of…

articles.title: Q&A: Why building math muscles remains important in the AI era
articles.content: John Urschel PhD ’21, the Class of 1956 Career Development Assistant Professor in the MIT Department of Mathematics, is no stranger to building muscle: Before earning his PhD at MIT, Urschel strengthened his offensive muscles as a lineman for the Baltimore Ravens. He remains committed to helping his students exercise, but now his focus is on critical thinking skills. In the classroom, Urschel shares with his students his lifelong love for solving puzzles, while honing their abilities to be strong qualitive thinkers — skills he argues will be essential in an artificial intelligence-enabled world. Urschel recently published two preprints on arXiv, one on the growth factor of random matrices , the other on worst-case behavior in Gaussian elimination , in which he used a combination of human insight and AI tools to solve problems that had stumped mathematicians for decades. That experience provided Urschel with new insights into the future of mathematics and higher education, and the enduring importance of the in-person, residential education offered on college campuses, where students can experience the importance of struggle, problem solving, and human connection. Urschel recently chatted with MIT News about education, AI, and mathematics; excerpts from the conversation follow. Q : What is it about studying math that you hope to share with your students? A : When I was very little, I loved solving puzzles, whether that’s Sudoku puzzles or Martin Gardner math puzzles or crossword puzzles. I think there’s something really enjoyable about being faced with some problem that you don’t quite understand, trying to get your bearings, trying to make your way through it, and finally gleaning some sort of understanding from it. That’s a process that I’ve enjoyed for as long as I can remember, and that’s the thing that I’ve really enjoyed most about math. When it comes to teaching, first, I want to help our students train themselves and hone their ability to solve problems and their ability to be strong quantitative thinkers. The second part, which is more specific to whichever course I’m teaching, is to help them assimilate the big ideas or tools or techniques or themes that help them become better problem solvers in that specific discipline. If they’re taking a course on a specific subject, the idea is for me to try to convey important fundamentals so that they can use that learned expertise to become better problem solvers out in the world. Q : You recently used AI to assist in solving two proofs. Can you talk a bit about the experience? A : These are the first two papers where I’ve ever touched the machine, and it does feel different. It’s not unlike having a collaborator, but it’s a collaborator who has access to unlimited resources, seemingly, and does certain things much, much faster than I ever could. In the same way that computers can do calculations much faster than any of us can, I think at this point it’s very clear that artificial intelligence systems can do certain types of mathematics much, much more efficiently than any of us can. Q : What was it like using AI to solve math problems? Was it just as rewarding? A : For me, personally, I would say that the feeling that I talked about of problem solving, of thinking your way through a problem, I find that that’s most joyful for me when I do that by myself, without AI. One thing that I think is really important is to have an independent sense of problem-solving ability, a sense of curiosity — this idea of building those mathematics muscles, which I think are important, even in the era of AI. Especially when you are talking with a machine, asking the machine for things, I think it’s very important to elevate the idea of understanding. If you’re talking to a machine, let’s say, and it gives you a proof of some mathematical fact, I think the true value in that proof comes from a human understanding and assimilating the way in which the machine combines certain mathematical ideas,…

articles.title: Learning the language of machine learning
articles.content: When deploying deep learning models in high-stakes scenarios, researchers would like to understand how they work. Today, this requires unraveling an enormously complex network of internal processing nodes to understand what the model knows and how it will likely behave in practice. Jacob Andreas would rather have the models explain themselves. The newly tenured associate professor develops techniques that enable artificial intelligence models to communicate accurately about what they learned from their training data, in language humans can understand. “Rather than needing to use all these external tools to try and understand what is going on under the hood, maybe we can train models to talk about themselves in a way that is accurate,” says Andreas, an associate professor in the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) and a member of the Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL). By studying how machines come to understand language, Andreas and his group work toward building intelligent systems that can learn about the world from human guidance and communicate effectively with human collaborators. They develop methods to make the training process more natural and efficient, so AI models learn in a way that is more like human learning. Ultimately, he and his group want to help people design more accurate and robust deep-learning models that are better suited for their intended application. “We used to debug systems just by looking at their parameters and figuring out whether they make sense or not. Now, we need ‘mind-reading tools’ that can take this really complicated neural computation and translate it for us because it is just not in a language that we, as humans, know how to speak,” he says. A love of language Andreas’ fascination with language blossomed at a young age. As a child growing up in the San Francisco Bay Area, he was a voracious reader of any book he could get his hands on. One such book, passed along to him by a family friend, contained a pivotal scene where the main character hacked into a computer system to save the day. That piqued his interest in computers. A few years later, his father brought home a simple BASIC Engine that Andreas could run on their home computer, and he started immersing himself in the world of computer programming. Andreas chose to major in computer science as an undergraduate at Columbia University but wasn’t sure if he wanted to pursue a career as a researcher, as a software engineer, or at a startup. His friends signed up for research projects in faculty labs, so Andreas figured he would try that, too. “I just blast emailed everyone in the computer science department who was working on anything vaguely AI-related, and the natural language processing faculty got back to me first. That is how I wound up in the field where I am now,” he says. Working in the lab of Michael Collins, the Vikram S. Pandit Professor of Computer Science at Columbia University, Andreas completed an undergraduate thesis project on machine translation. His project involved adapting existing statistical techniques for representing the meaning of language into more powerful AI systems that could translate passages of text. “I always felt like these deeper questions about how thought works or how to model the world were closer to the surface in language processing problems than in the other tasks that AI people were working on at the time,” he recalls. A seismic shift He wanted to keep exploring deep questions, so Andreas enrolled in graduate school at the University of California at Berkeley to pursue a career as an academic researcher. Before starting his PhD studies, he spent a year earning a master’s degree at Cambridge University in England. In that historic environment, he was inspired to contemplate the nature of language learning as he worked on computational translation problems. articles.summaryEn: Researchers are seeking to gain a better understanding of deep learning models in high-stakes situations, and Jacob Andreas has developed techniques that allow these models to communicate in human-understandable language about what they have learned from training data. He and his team aim to enable AI systems to interact more effectively with humans and learn in a way that is similar to human learning.
insightsFa: محققان در تلاشند تا لایه‌های پیچیده مدل‌های یادگیری عمیق را درک کنند.
Jacob Andreas روش‌هایی را برای ارتباط مؤثرتر هوش مصنوعی با انسان‌ها توسعه داده است.
هدف ایجاد سیستمی است که یادگیری AI را مشابه یادگیری انسانی کند.
لزوم استفاده از ابزارهایی برای درک محتوای پیچیده پردازش‌های عصبی.
پیشرفت‌های جدید به طراحی مدل‌های عمیق‌تر و قابل اعتمادتر کمک می‌کند.
articles.whyItMattersFa: این خبر مهم است زیرا فهم دقیق عملکرد مدل‌های یادگیری عمیق به بهبود تعامل انسان و هوش مصنوعی و همچنین توسعه سیستم‌های هوشمند کارآمدتر کمک می‌کند.

articles.content: Baidu Inc. chief Robin Li sees an increasingly urgent need for better monetization of artificial intelligence if heavy investments in the technology are to pay off.

articles.title: Google’s ‘Pixel virtual gamepad’ is finally rolling out for foldable Pixels
articles.content: Credit: Nick Fernandez / Android Authority TL;DR Google is finally starting to roll out “Pixel virtual gamepad,” which lets users play supported Android games using on-screen controls when their Pixel Fold is open. This appears to be the virtual controller Google announced as part of Android 17’s Foldable Gaming Mode. It looks like Google is finally moving ahead with an Android 17’s features that was announced months ago. The company’s latest Google Play Store release notes mention something called the “Pixel virtual gamepad,” suggesting that Android 17’s “Foldable Gaming Mode” is finally making its way to users.
articles.author: Adamya Sharma
articles.fingerprint: finally foldable gamepad google out pixel pixels rolling virtual
articles.titleFa: گیم‌پد مجازی پیکسل گوگل بالاخره برای گوشی‌های تاشو عرضه می‌شود

articles.title: Impact of US Move to Curb Chip Access
articles.content: Managing Editor for Asian Equities at Bloomberg News Lianting Tu says tighter access to chips could constrain AI model training in China and potentially slow sales growth for AI cloud businesses. That could have a knock-on effect on data-center expansion and demand for Chinese hardware companies, some of which supply Nvidia, as the Trump administration moves to limit countries from providing Chinese companies remote access to advanced artificial intelligence chips and servers. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.summaryEn: New U.S. restrictions on access to advanced chips may affect AI model training in China and potentially slow sales growth for AI cloud businesses. This could have indirect impacts on data center expansion and demand for Chinese hardware companies.

Google Messages could once again make it easier to keep your inbox organized by bringing back conversation categories, a feature that existed in the app years ago.

articles.title: 350 tech jobs hammered as TCS takes over work at iconic Australian retailer
articles.content: Indian tech giant Tata Consultancy Services has a new client, iconic Australian retailer Bunnings Warehouse which has made a third of its IT department redundant. Bunnings is Australia’s equivalent of big box hardware retailers Home Depot and B&Q and earlier today advised its IT teams to attend a town hall meeting. The Register understands the invitation to that meeting was sent twice, after the first effort contained an error. We hear from staff that the botched invitation was taken as a clue of what was to happen next, namely the announcement of 230 redundancies plus an end to 120 contracted roles. The town hall meeting was not interactive, with a Bunnings rep speaking from a script and not taking questions. Staff whose roles will end then received an email inviting them to a meeting. Bunnings, whose logo is a hammer, has tried to explain the decision in a statement that says, “We need a technology model and partner that keeps pace with our customers so that we can continue to deliver the service, value and helpful advice people expect from us.” “These changes reflect the way customers are choosing to shop and the increasingly competitive retail environment,” the statement adds, before pointing out “Bunnings is already investing in technology and digital experiences to respond to these changes, earlier this year becoming the first Australian retailer to launch an AI-powered shopping agent using Google's Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience platform through Buddy.” Some of the TCS workers Bunnings is hiring will work in Australia. Others will work from India and the Philippines. While Bunnings follows the template of a big box retailer, each of its stores allows charities and community groups to run fundraising barbeques in its forecourt every weekend. Those barbeques are a significant source of income for many non-profits and have earned the chain a broad social license. The hardware barn is so well-known that children’s TV show Bluey – the most viewed program of 2024 and 2025 in the US – gently parodied it as "Hammerbarn" it in an episode. The Register mentions this because we understand the reference to TCS staff helping to deliver the Bunnings experience has gone down badly, as the chain’s employees wonder how offshore workers who have not experienced its stores and atmosphere can deliver a service that preserves its culture. Bunnings says its new IT operating model will commence in July 2027 and that “Impacted team members will be supported in their roles through Christmas, with any changes taking effect in the new year.” The company’s IT team will still employ around 500 people. These job losses add to a rotten year for Australia’s tech scene, which this year saw local heroes Canva and Atlassian farewell hundreds of staff. Iconic Australian airline Qantas last week outsourced hundreds of jobs to India through Accenture. ®
articles.author: Simon Sharwood
articles.fingerprint: 350 australian hammered iconic jobs over retailer takes tcs tech work

Bunnings، با بهره‌گیری از فناوری‌های جدید و ایجاد تجربه‌های دیجیتال، در تلاش است تا خود را با تغییرات بازار و نیازهای مشتریان هماهنگ کند.

insightsFa: TCS به همراه Bunnings Warehouse در استرالیا به کار مشغول شده است.

Bunnings به دنبال بهبود تجربه مشتری با استفاده از فناوری‌های جدید است.

Bunnings در حال حاضر در حال سرمایه گذاری در فناوری‌های دیجیتال است.

articles.title: China AI Star Sinks 85% From Peak as Chip Fears Hit Model Makers
articles.content: Few stocks rode China’s artificial intelligence frenzy as spectacularly as model developer Z.AI Co. Now, its dramatic reversal is laying bare the vulnerabilities facing the country’s AI upstarts.
articles.author: Jeanny Yu
articles.fingerprint: china chip fears hit makers model peak sinks star

نگرانی‌ها درباره کمبود تراشه، تأثیر منفی بر روی تولیدکنندگان مدل‌های هوش مصنوعی دارد.
بازار هوش مصنوعی چین در حال تجربه نوسانات شدید است.

articles.title: Just 400 US Data Centers Use More Electricity Than Michigan
articles.content: An anonymous reader quotes a report from Wired: Just 400 hyperscale data centers connected in the US used as much electricity as the state of Michigan in a single year, new Harvard research has found. The study, published Monday in Nature Sustainability, also finds that the majority of that electricity was generated using fossil fuels, and data center emissions are three times higher than they were before the AI boom. Federal and state governments do not track data center use separate from the rest of the power sector, despite mounting projections that data centers are putting serious strain on the American power grid. Individual data centers' power use is often considered proprietary business information, and data center operators and utilities do not have to disclose specific numbers to the public. The Harvard study specifically focuses on hyperscale data centers -- the largest types of facilities, which have become flashpoints in community opposition across the country. While often used for AI inference or training, not all of the hyperscalers surveyed in this study are being used for AI. [...] To assemble their dataset, the Harvard researchers put together a list of 403 hyperscale data centers around the country that were operational between May 2024 and April 2025 using a mix of industry research and satellite data. The team then modeled these facilities' energy use in a variety of scenarios and calculated the energy mix of the regional grids to estimate individual facilities' carbon emissions. Not all regions were created equal: Data centers in Virginia, Oregon, Ohio, and Iowa -- the first of which is home to Data Center Alley -- were responsible for more than 50 percent of the energy use in the study. The report notes that these findings may already be outdated. "Some of the massive campuses being proposed today are substantially larger than the typical facility in our dataset," says Gianluca Guidi, a postdoctoral research fellow at Harvard's T. H. Chan School of Public Health and the lead author of the study. The study also excludes onsite power generation, a rapidly growing trend that BloombergNEF estimates could increase overall U.S. emissions by 10% if all proposed projects are built. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.content: Xi Qiao, UBS financial advisor and managing director, said Nvidia faces a particularly difficult backdrop ahead of earnings, including tougher U.S. export restrictions and concerns surrounding Jensen Huang. Qiao advised investors to stay invested while diversifying across sectors, regions and asset classes. articles.title: Black Friday hasn’t even started but I’m already callin’ it: Sony’s WH-1000XM6 at a record-low price is the best headphones deal of the season
articles.content: The Amazon Black Friday Sale is only in its first few hours, but it’s already delivered what I reckon is going to be one of the best deals we’ll see this entire sales period, with a huge AU$279.05 saving on the superb Sony WH-1000XM6 headphones — that’s the lowest-ever price we’ve seen in Australia. Sony’s flagship cans are roughly a year and a half old, and in that time, I’ve rarely found them discounted. And if they were, it wasn’t by much. Fortunately, this offer on what I consider to be the best headphones in Australia right now makes them an absolute must-consider for anyone looking for a true gem of a pair of headphones. • Follow our live coverage of all the latest Amazon Black Friday deals and discounts Right now, you can grab the incredible Sony WH-1000XM6 with 40% off at Amazon, dropping them to a new all-time Aussie low. These headphones offer stunning, balanced audio output, top-tier touch controls, ergonomic comfort, and noise-nixing ANC. They'd make the perfect gift, or why not just treat yourself if you're traveling a lot this gift-giving season? View Deal The slight caveat to this deal is that the lowest price only applies to the black variant. Other colours do get a discount, but only to AU$495. That’s still a decent price for the talented over-ears, but obviously nowhere near as attractive as the AU$419.95 for the black model. You only need a quick glance over our Sony WH-1000XM6 review to see how highly we rate these Sony flagship headphones, and we’ve even put together some comparison pieces to prove how capable they are. You can, for instance, check out how the Sony WH-1000XM6 compares to the Apple AirPods Max 2 — themselves also on sale right now . Sony has long been known for producing top-performing pairs of headphones, and the 1000X series has proven particularly popular for good reason. This latest set represents the company’s decades of expertise, combining a travel-friendly, fold away design with a wonderfully balanced audio performance, and some truly effective ANC. At their full price of AU$699, I personally struggle to recommend them when it’s possible to find other pairs for a lot less, but honestly, this discount solves that dilemma in a big way.

articles.title: US marijuana farms are becoming AI data centers — they already have the water and power needed, and with weed revenues falling, it seems an ideal switch
articles.content: Falling cannabis revenues are pushing growers to reconsider cultivation properties Former marijuana farms have infrastructure that could support smaller AI data centers AI demand is giving struggling cannabis properties an unexpected commercial purpose The expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure is creating another possible use for facilities originally constructed to support large-scale indoor marijuana production, new reports have claimed. At the same time, declining marijuana prices are forcing some American cannabis growers to reconsider the future of their cultivation properties as operating costs continue rising. Several former and current operators are therefore examining whether existing cultivation buildings could accommodate small data centers without requiring entirely new construction. Existing infrastructure makes cannabis properties attractive to data center operators Cannabis cultivation requires substantial electricity and water supplies, particularly for indoor operations involving artificial lighting, ventilation, cooling, and humidity regulation. These requirements have left some facilities with electrical connections, industrial cooling equipment, and water infrastructure that could reduce the initial requirements for establishing computing operations. In Kalamazoo, Michigan, a 32,850-square-foot cultivation property already has electrical capacity of 1.5 megawatts, with considerable room for expansion. Its electricity supply could reach 2.5 megawatts within one year, while longer-term improvements could eventually increase available capacity to 15 megawatts. The property also has fiber internet connectivity and an advanced heating, ventilation, and air conditioning system suitable for maintaining controlled indoor temperatures. These characteristics could make former cultivation facilities attractive to companies seeking smaller computing locations instead of constructing new industrial complexes. “For some reason, there's a lot more cannabis grown in Arizona than Arizonans use. And so, a lot of folks are getting out of that business, like myself, at least on the cultivation side. But these facilities can potentially be repurposed to be mini data center nodes,” said Moe Asnani, former owner of two D2 Dispensaries in Tucson, Arizona. Conversion still carries substantial obstacles The proposed conversion, sometimes called adaptive reuse, could also help address opposition against constructing large computing complexes in residential communities. Tucson City Council member Paul Cunningham considers existing industrial properties a potentially more acceptable alternative to developing entirely new facilities. “Data centers are dirty words, and everybody knows that. And no one wants to build a brand-new data center anywhere,” Cunningham said. However, converting cultivation buildings does not automatically make them suitable for commercial computing operations. Operators must consider electricity prices, fiber connectivity, and taxation before selecting properties. Computing facilities can require two to three times the electrical capacity available at many cultivation properties, making infrastructure improvements particularly important. Such upgrades could require as much as five years, potentially delaying projects and weakening the financial attraction of purchasing otherwise inexpensive agricultural properties. Smaller installations must also contend with restrictive zoning regulations, construction restrictions, neighborhood opposition, and potentially expensive electricity infrastructure improvements. Their operating economics could become particularly challenging as AI processors advance, requiring frequent hardware replacements to maintain competitive computing performance. Large operators also benefit from purchasing equipment in substantial quantities, whereas smaller installations could face higher individual hardware costs during subsequent upgrades. articles.title: Turtle Beach Command Series MC7 review: great performance, weak design
articles.content: Turtle Beach Command Series MC7 review The Turtle Beach Command Series MC7 gaming mouse left me with one question after testing it: just because you can do something, does that mean you should ? See, the Turtle Beach Command Series MC7 comes equipped with a touchscreen — just like the brand's Command Series keyboards. I can understand having a few useful shortcuts and commands available at the tap of a screen on your keyboard — especially if you’re a streamer or competitive gamer. But it just feels straight up unnecessary on a mouse. First of all, the touchscreen is pretty small and didn’t feel particularly natural to use with my thumb. What’s more, a lot of the features available — like adjusting DPI or polling rate — can just be mapped to the customizable ‘M’ buttons scattered across the mouse. Sure, the touchscreen enables you to launch a gaming overlay or media controls, but again, it feels like these could be tied to button controls or keyboard shortcuts. Don’t get me wrong, the touchscreen is nice and bright, it’s responsive, and the software is easy to get started with after downloading the Swarm II app, but overall, the interface feels superfluous. Anyway, let’s look past the touchscreen for now, and assess how the MC7 fares against the best gaming mice in terms of performance. And luckily, it does pretty well in this department. From the specs alone, you can tell that the MC7 is oriented towards competitive gamers. You’re getting true 8K polling with 0.125ms latency, a 30K DPI ‘Owl-Eye’ optical sensor, and Titan Optical Switches with adjustable debounce and, according to Turtle Beach, “a 150 million-click lifespan”. But how does that translate into actual use? Well, I tried playing Counter-Strike 2 , and had a very good experience overall. While you can get higher sensitivity from mice like the Steelseries Sensei Pro , I found the sensor to be excellent, with impressive speed and tracking. The 8K polling is another great feature, and helped me aim with great precision, with ultra-smooth movement. The Titan Optical Switches also felt highly satisfying and snappy, with a pleasant mechanical sound to them. The 4D scroll wheel is pretty cool too, and can dynamically snap from small steps to free-spin scrolling — plus you can click it left or right for seamless navigation. (Image credit: Future) What I would say, though, is that some may find the MC7 to be a little unwieldy. While its sloped design felt pretty comfortable to me, I will say that it's a pretty large mouse — and quite heavy at that. Those with smaller hands may want to steer clear, and if you prefer a lightweight feel, this mouse will likely feel too hefty for you. On the topic of design, I have to say that the MC7 is one of the less attractive mice I’ve tested in my time at TechRadar. The bronze details feel a little garish alongside the purple touchscreen, black body and LED lighting — it’s all just a bit messy. The mouse also uses a strange combination of boldly angular and rounded segments, giving it an awkward form. That is to say that it feels like the MC7 is having a bit of an identity crisis, and I wish it was at least a bit easier on the eye. I feel like I’ve bashed this mouse quite a lot, so I want to return to the positives for a moment. The Turtle Beach Command Series MC7 has an absolutely brilliant hot-swappable battery system, which essentially gives you infinite playtime. The wireless transmitter houses a battery that can charge while you use your mouse, and when your battery eventually dies, you can swap the transmitter battery right in. Other than the few seconds you’ll take to switch the batteries, you’ll get unbroken play. Something else that impressed me was the sheer number of features on offer. You can pick between a 2.4GHz wireless, Bluetooth, or wired connection, providing exceptional versatility. The Swarm II companion software also opens up a lot of options, like button mapping, touchscreen customization, and lighting adjustments.…
articles.author: Harry Padoan

articles.title: US extends chip sale restrictions to more Asian countries to reduce risk of ‘diversion’ to China
articles.content: The US Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has decided to ban remote access to certain GPUs and servers running in datacenters located in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil. The agency has also introduced a requirement to secure a license before selling what it describes as “advanced super intelligence (SI) chips and servers” that are sufficiently powerful to “be used for training or running of advanced SI models” into the five nations. The interim final rule [PDF] containing the new regulations says they’re needed “to prevent certain foreign actors from leveraging advanced computing power based on US technology to threaten US national security and foreign policy interests.” Similar language can be found in previous US bans on sales of GPUs and other advanced tech to China, which Washington fears will use advanced tech to improve its military capabilities. US authorities understood that export bans wouldn’t prevent Chinese entities from renting GPUs housed elsewhere. So from 2021 to 2024, Washington introduced a series of regulations that required US-based clouds to make sure they didn’t serve Chinese customers. No such obligation existed for cloud operators elsewhere, which created a market for resources that Chinese customers could access from afar. It is widely felt that datacenter building booms in Malaysia and Thailand, both of which are generally on good terms with China, aimed to cater to Middle Kingdom customers who wanted to rent GPUs they could not import. Megapseed – whose former employee Alice Huang had an intimate relationship with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and may have been a Chinese intelligence asset – built datacenters in Malaysia and was suspected of catering largely to offshore customers. Neil Shah, vice president of research at analyst firm Counterpoint, said the new rules shift the regulatory burden of complying with export controls from hardware manufacturers to cloud operators. “Data center operators in hubs such as Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia will now face massive ‘Know Your Customer's Workload’ requirements,” he told The Register by email, likening it to the KYC restrictions imposed on financial services firms. “They must prove to US regulators that their compute is not being funneled back to embargoed nations, or risk losing their own access to US silicon.” He feels the new rules represent “a severe short-term compute bottleneck for Chinese tech giants” and “a massive long-term catalyst for decoupling.” “Washington is forcing domestic capital and engineering talent to double down on full-stack sovereign alternatives, accelerating ecosystems like Huawei's Ascend.” Shah’s observation came days after Alibaba decided to spin out its T-Head chip design unit, which it described as “a leading provider of full-stack data center chips which enable system-level compute solutions in China.” That description suggests Alibaba doesn’t think T-Head has strong prospects of selling its wares outside China. It remains to be seen if the new BIS rules will slow datacenter development across Asia and Brazil. All five nations the US has regulated are all enjoying the economic impact of the AI boom. They’re also trying to manage its impact. Singapore limits datacenter construction, as befits a tiny and resource-constrained island nation. Malaysia is very much open for business but has introduced increasingly strict building codes and requirements to minimize energy and water consumption. Thailand recently introduced new regulations that new builds of large datacenters must take place in designated industrial zones. Indonesia also has strong regulations but is not currently a major datacenter hub. Brazil requires datacenter operators to reserve at least 10 percent of capacity for local users, suggesting some operators are more interested in offshore customers. articles.content: Keychron makes a lot of keyboards, but the latest Ultra 8K line is the peak of their offering, while the K2 keeps those specs and premium design affordable. Keychron K2 Ultra 8K review I'll be honest, I had to comb through the specs page to understand exactly what was different about the Keychron K2 Ultra 8K versus the Q1 Ultra 8K I reviewed recently . That's a compliment considering this keyboard is half the price. When shopping for Keychron keyboards, it is best to understand what each portion of the name represents. In this case, the K2 is a step down from the Q-series thanks to its metal frame versus full-metal body, plus some other small differences. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums

articles.title: Russian hackers target Romanian servers to steal NATO, EU emails
articles.content: Cereal malware secretly searched Romanian government emails for NATO and EU connections ESET discovered previously undocumented software linked to Russia's Turla hacking group Hackers exploited Microsoft Exchange systems to conceal their email collection activities Cyberespionage hackers allegedly linked to Russia infiltrated the Romanian government email servers, seeking correspondence involving NATO and European Union institutions. The operation relied on previously unseen malicious software ESET researchers named Cereal, according to the cybersecurity company's published investigation. Rather than sending stolen messages immediately to an outside server, the intruders exploited the victim's own email environment to conceal their activity. A covert toolset searched institutional correspondence ESET said the intrusion began on December 23, 2025, after investigators had identified the same software in Kazakhstan the previous month. The malicious package contained several .NET components capable of receiving instructions, executing code in memory, and examining an infected organization's internal structure. One module, called CerealBox, searched messages for addresses associated with NATO and European Union bodies, then applied filters to identify selected correspondence. Emails containing Microsoft Word documents or PDF files were among those selected, after which the software packaged and encrypted copies for collection. This approach allowed the operators to obtain specific material without indiscriminately copying every message stored within the compromised organization's mail environment. ESET described the software as unusual because its methods relied on detailed knowledge of Exchange systems and unconventional .NET execution techniques. The researchers said the malicious code also used legitimate server functions, reducing the need for communications with infrastructure controlled directly by the attackers. That arrangement could make detection more difficult because security teams might see activity occurring through systems their organizations already depend upon. For institutions managing sensitive diplomatic correspondence, secure email protections must therefore include scrutiny of internal server activity, not simply suspicious external messages. ESET links the activity to Russia's Turla group ESET attributed the operation to Turla with high confidence, pointing to overlapping tools and similarities with malicious programs previously associated with the group. Turla is widely assessed by cybersecurity researchers as connected to Russia's Federal Security Service, which handles internal security and intelligence operations. The group has a history of pursuing government organizations, including prominent Ukrainian institutions, and has operated across Eastern Europe and Central Asia. According to ESET, around 70% of the countries previously affected by Turla were former Soviet republics or former communist states. Romania's location on NATO's eastern edge makes the discovery particularly significant, given the country's exposure to security tensions. Romanian authorities have previously faced digital attacks, including a 2025 campaign against defense manufacturers supplying equipment or support to Ukraine. Shortly after the war in Ukraine started, denial-of-service incidents disrupted websites belonging to Romanian public bodies and financial institutions. The latest compromise adds another example of espionage activity directed at institutions in a country supporting Ukraine and belonging to NATO. ESET identified the malware, but the company did not disclose how many emails the hackers managed to steal. Via Defense News
articles.author: Efosa Udinmwen

articles.title: Everything New in iOS 27.3 Beta 2
articles.content: Apple released the second beta of iOS 27.3 today, and like the first beta , it has several major new features. There are improvements to the iPhone Duo , tweaks to apps, new Siri features, and more. iPhone Duo Face Unlock Apple added a new option to quickly unlock the iPhone Duo using the front-facing camera. The option is only available when the ‌iPhone Duo‌ is closed, and it can only be used on the Lock Screen. Authenticating with Touch ID is required for Apple Pay purchases and for accessing passwords and logins. Unlocking with the camera requires recent ‌Touch ID‌ or passcode authentication, and ‌Touch ID‌ is required again after about 45 minutes of inactivity. Unlocking with the front-facing camera does not work when the ‌iPhone Duo‌ is open, presumably because the under-display camera is not high enough quality. The face unlock feature can be turned on in the Settings app under ‌Touch ID‌ and Passcode. iPhone Duo Lock When Closed Apple added an option to lock the ‌iPhone Duo‌ when it's closed instead of transferring content to the front display. Close to Lock can be turned on in the Display and Brightness section of the Settings app. Siri AI There's a new "Ask About Page" feature for ‌Siri‌ AI that lets ‌Siri‌ see the entire content of a webpage, even if it's not currently in view on the screen. ‌Siri‌ AI can also now access Health data when given permission, and control over smart home products has improved. Apple Intelligence and Siri AI Usage Limits iOS 27.3 introduces the Apple Intelligence usage limits cxdApple has been warning about for months. ‌Siri‌ AI and ‌Apple Intelligence‌ features that use server-side processing will now have daily usage limits on a per-device basis. Extra access is tied to 200GB and higher iCloud + plans. The 200GB plan gives up to 2x usage, the 2TB plan is up to 5x, the 6TB plan is up to 10x, and the 12TB plan is up to 20x. Limits apply to complex ‌Siri‌ AI requests that involve multiple steps, image generation and editing tools, AI workflows and automations in Shortcuts, and third-party apps that use Apple Foundation Models in Private Cloud Compute. More information can be found in our article on the new limits . Calendar The Calendar app has an updated layout with the options for searching and adding an event moved to the bottom of the app. The "Today" button that takes you to the current date has also been updated to show the date. Apple TV App Podcasts Video podcast episodes are now available in the Apple TV app. Only video podcasts that are free will show up in the ‌Apple TV‌ app. Apple News+ Puzzles Apple News + Puzzles are expanding to Australian, UK, and French-Canadian ‌Apple News‌+ subscribers. Subscribers in Australia get access to a daily quick crossword, crossword mini, Sudoku, Quartiles, and Emoji Game. UK subscribers get the daily quick crossword, crossword mini, and Sudoku, while French-Canadian subscribers can play Quartiles and Emoji Game. Weather App There are 10 new weather condition symbols in the Weather app, but Apple doesn't appear to be using them yet. The Weather app gets 10 new weather-condition symbols in iOS 27.3 beta 2. https://t.co/1c5W4n5gKn — pdfu (@itspdfu) November 16, 2026 Home App The Home app has an "Unrecognized People" section that limits how guests can use Safari and ‌Siri‌ on Apple home devices. Apple Music There's code in Apple Music for an album release countdown , but it doesn't appear to be active yet. Related Roundups: iOS 27 , iPadOS 27 Related Forum: iOS 27 This article, " Everything New in iOS 27.3 Beta 2 " first appeared on MacRumors.com Discuss this article in our forums

articles.title: The smart-heating, auto-leveling Elegoo Saturn 4 Ultra 16K 3D printer gets a $250 discount
articles.content: The Elegoo Saturn 4 Ultra 16K resin 3D printer has dropped from $649.99 to $399 in the Black Friday sale. That’s a hefty saving - around 39% - on a printer that’s been built to churn out highly detailed models, so it’s ideal if you want to print miniatures and other intricate prints. Today’s best Elegoo Saturn 4 Ultra 16K deal Saturn 4 Ultra 16K: was $649.99 now $399.99 The US Elegoo store is offering the printer for $399 as part of its Black Friday sale. This offer applies to the standalone printer, not bundles that include washing and curing equipment. Don’t fret if you want a bundle or accessories, though: Elegoo’s extensive Black Friday sale also includes discounts on bundles that include post-processing machines and resin, and discounts are also available on accessories like build plates and PFA film. View Deal Why we recommend the Elegoo Saturn 4 Ultra 16K The Saturn 4 Ultra 16K’s headline feature is a 10-inch monochrome LCD with 16K resolution, which means that you get an impressive XY resolution of 14 x 19 microns. The unit also has a generous 211.68 x 118.37 x 220mm build volume and print speeds of up to 150mm/h. It also serves up automated bed leveling, a heated resin tank, and an AI camera to monitor your prints. Price context and historical value The Saturn’s $399 price is a hefty 39% discount from the original $649.99. It’s a substantial discount if you’ve been considering a high-resolution resin printer. That’s a great start, and we’d also point interested buyers to the variety of bundle and accessory deals available with this model. They may enable you to put together a purchase that better suits your needs. Should you buy it? ✅ Buy the Saturn 4 Ultra 16K if… you want detailed resin prints for your models and miniatures - alongside generous build volume and useful automation ❌ Skip the Saturn 4 Ultra 16K if… you want your next 3D printer to be a low-maintenance model. Resin printing needs more handling, cleaning, curing, and ventilation than filament.

articles.title: NYT Connections hints and answers for Tuesday, November 17 (game #1255)
articles.content: Looking for a different day? A new NYT Connections puzzle appears at midnight each day for your time zone – which means that some people are always playing 'today's game' while others are playing 'yesterday's'. If you're looking for Monday's puzzle instead then click here: NYT Connections hints and answers for Monday, November 16 (game #1254) . Good morning! Let's play Connections, the NYT's clever word game that challenges you to group answers in various categories. It can be tough, so read on if you need Connections hints. What should you do once you've finished? Why, play some more word games of course. I've also got daily Strands hints and answers and Quordle hints and answers articles if you need help for those too, while Marc's Wordle today page covers the original viral word game. SPOILER WARNING: Information about NYT Connections today is below, so don't read on if you don't want to know the answers. NYT Connections today (game #1255) - today's words (Image credit: New York Times) Today's NYT Connections words are… KINGPIN BLACKBIRD FLOCK AIRPLANE COME TOGETHER THEM PIE VALLEY PENNY LANE RYE HELP GATHER SHAZAM MASKED BALL ASSEMBLE SIXPENCE NYT Connections today (game #1255) - hint #1 - group hints What are some clues for today's NYT Connections groups? YELLOW: All in one place GREEN: Featured in a nursery rhyme BLUE: Movies with a grammatical link PURPLE: Indoor activity featuring strikes and spares Need more clues? We're firmly in spoiler territory now, but read on if you want to know what the four theme answers are for today's NYT Connections puzzles… NYT Connections today (game #1255) - hint #2 - group answers What are the answers for today's NYT Connections groups? YELLOW: CONVENE GREEN: THINGS IN "SING A SONG OF SIXPENCE" BLUE: FILMS WITH "!" IN THE TITLE PURPLE: ENDING IN BOWLING TERMS Right, the answers are below, so DO NOT SCROLL ANY FURTHER IF YOU DON'T WANT TO SEE THEM. NYT Connections today (game #1255) - the answers (Image credit: New York Times) The answers to today's Connections, game #1255, are… YELLOW: CONVENE: ASSEMBLE, COME TOGETHER, FLOCK, GATHER GREEN: THINGS IN "SING A SONG OF SIXPENCE": BLACKBIRD, PIE, RYE, SIXPENCE BLUE: FILMS WITH "!" IN THE TITLE: AIRPLANE, HELP, SHAZAM, THEM PURPLE: ENDING IN BOWLING TERMS: KINGPIN, MASKED BALL, PENNY LANE, VALLEY My rating: Hard My score: 3 mistakes Of course I collected together the four random Beatles songs — BLACKBIRD, HELP, PENNY LANE and COME TOGETHER — and immediately regretted it, but this was far from the end of my mistakes. In both instances I was on the right track. I knew the green group was something to do with a nursery rhyme I couldn’t quite grasp, so had FLOCK instead of RYE before realizing what we were looking for. Then I thought we were looking for spoof films, not realizing the connection was exclamation marks, so included KINGPIN instead of THEM. Fortunately, amid these mistakes I somehow managed to GATHER four groups — well, three if we’re being completely honest. Yesterday's NYT Connections answers (Monday, November 16, 2026, game #1254) YELLOW: SUMMER _____: BLOCKBUSTER, CAMP, SAUSAGE, SCHOOL GREEN: SPRING ______: CHICKEN, CLEANING, ONION, WATER BLUE: WINTER ______: GARDEN, GLOVES, MELON, WONDERLAND PURPLE: FALL ____: ASLEEP, FOLIAGE, GUY, IN LOVE What is NYT Connections? NYT Connections is one of several increasingly popular word games made by the New York Times. It challenges you to find groups of four items that share something in common, and each group has a different difficulty level: green is easy, yellow a little harder, blue often quite tough and purple usually very difficult. On the plus side, you don't technically need to solve the final one, as you'll be able to answer that one by a process of elimination. What's more, you can make up to four mistakes, which gives you a little bit of breathing room. articles.title: JPMorgan Chase Glitch Disrupts Online Banking Across Major US Banks
articles.content: A software bug at JPMorgan Chase has disrupted online banking services Monday, triggering transaction delays for thousands of customers at Chase and other major U.S. banks. "JPMorgan Chase has experienced a temporary issue related to a software bug in an on-premise hardware system -- it is not cyber-related," said Joe Evangelisti, spokesman for the bank. "This is not a systemic issue -- other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us," he added. The Associated Press reports: Monday's technical issues seem to be centered at Chase customers and customers at other banks trying to transact with Chase. Those banks, including Bank of America and Citigroup, were not having issues with their banking services. A spokesman for U.S. Bank said its systems are not directly impacted but that "clients attempting to send or receive Zelle payments with another financial institution may experience transaction delays." Developing... Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Microsoft outage: A cascading failure that started with an undetected bug
articles.content: Following a roughly day-long global outage of many Microsoft services last week, Microsoft on Monday issued a preliminary post-incident report that identified multiple causes for the issues, including the admission that the environment used to test the underlying problematic software update did not match the actual infrastructure it would run on. The report, a summary of which was posted on social media by Microsoft EVP Charles Lamanna, identified some of the factors that cascaded to cause the outage. “A latent defect caused servers to become overwhelmed and unresponsive under certain load conditions,” the report said, adding, “this defect was the result of a fix that was prepared specifically for Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers.” Its deployment began in July, and, the report said, “for more than three months, the change was deployed worldwide without impact.” Microsoft admitted that, although it did test the change before deployment, its test environment didn’t match reality. “Our normal load testing did not detect the latent issue because the different traffic and SKU mix used in our test labs,” it said. “The contention issue is worsened on machines with more cores and newer hardware; whereas our load testing tended to focus on our weaker hardware SKUs with fewer cores.” A surge in traffic caused by unrelated issues also helped trigger the problem and delay it from being fixed, the company explained. “Within Microsoft 365, we maintain two independent and heterogenous network gateway systems designed for isolation and high availability,” Microsoft said. “This allows many Microsoft 365 services to fail to/from them during outages or disruptions. Approximately fifteen hours before the outage, Teams failed over from the alternative networking gateway to the primary gateway that also supports Exchange Online. This increased the load on the networking gateway and changed its traffic patterns.” To make things worse, the report said, “nearly 14% of server capacity for the networking gateway was out of service due to an unrelated issue from the previous day.” Microsoft did not provide details of that unrelated issue. The combination of those elements led to the outage. Cascading failure “The increased load and the reduced server capacity caused the network gateway to encounter the latent bug from July,” Microsoft said. “This caused requests to build up until servers ultimately stopped responding.” And although, when servers lose connectivity, traffic management systems automatically route users to other healthy endpoints, the redirected traffic made the problem more likely to occur on the remaining functional endpoints. “This caused a cascading failure from server to server as the same amount of load was spread across fewer servers,” the report said. “In less than two hours, the previously unknown defect was encountered across our fleet and rendered them unresponsive. At its lowest, more than 80% of servers were unresponsive.” That cascading series of problems worked against Microsoft as it tried to resolve the issue, because as servers were brought back online, the deluge of waiting traffic triggered the bug and they became unresponsive again. “Our normally automated recovery processes were not designed to restore service from this broad unresponsive state,” Microsoft said. “Additionally, since the main code defect was a latent bug from several months previous, our normal rollback, flighting, and feature flags were unable to quickly revert the change.” Explanations still needed Consultants said that Microsoft overall did an admirable job of trying to get systems back into service, but added that the vendor needs to further explain why its testing environment did not match reality. “I believe this is a risk inherent in the business model that can’t be mitigated with some clever workaround,” said David Shipley , CEO of Beauceron Security. “Microsoft literally did everything I could ever think of, and it all failed in a…

articles.title: California sues OpenAI for misleading public about AI safety
articles.content: California Attorney General Rob Bonta has sued OpenAI under the state's unfair competition and public nuisance laws, for allegedly misleading and endangering the public by deploying unsafe AI models. The lawsuit [PDF], filed in California Superior Court, follows the compromise of Hugging Face's infrastructure and other cyber incidents OpenAI's experimental models caused when taking autonomous actions without authorization or supervision. "While narratives about the Hugging Face attack have evoked science fiction fantasies of rogue AI systems run amok, let me be clear: the Hugging Face attack was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability — and this was only one of 80 known incidents," said Attorney General Bonta. At a press conference , Bonta added: "OpenAI disregarded public safety, knowingly tested potentially dangerous AI models without proper oversight and safety measures, and misled consumers and the public." The legal salvo comes after Bonta in September sent OpenAI a letter seeking information about these agentic attacks. According to the complaint, "OpenAI failed to substantially comply" with the investigatory subpoena. In August, 15 states led by Iowa – and excluding California – issued a joint demand for OpenAI to provide information about how its models hacked Hugging Face. OpenAI did not respond to a request for comment. Bonta's office previously joined with Delaware Attorney General Kathy Jennings to urge OpenAI to do more for children's safety in light of reports that its models produced sexually inappropriate output. California did not, however, join the eight states that sued OpenAI in October over alleged misrepresentations about child safety. Florida and Texas have also made child safety claims. Child safety plays well politically; California appears to be the first state to demand more accountability toward the general public. Bonta's lawsuit, in a state that has largely accommodated the AI industry for the sake of economic benefits and political contributions , suggests that California officials may be more willing to bite the hand that feeds. The many Democratic victories in the US midterm elections may also be a factor, as pundits feel voters swung to give lawmakers license to regulate the unpopular AI industry. At his press conference, Bonta made sure to convey that he wants accountability without smothering the AI industry in costly regulation. "Let me be clear," he said. "I believe in the technological and economic power of AI. If we're able to address these very high stakes safety issues, AI could lead to some of the most incredible improvements in the history of humankind." AI is yet to deliver those incredible improvements. It has delivered deepfakes, huge quantities of cybersecurity vulnerabilities, and the permissionless resale of past intellectual labor, plus high energy and RAM prices. As well as some productivity gains in certain areas like coding, albeit at an unknown cost to future job markets. But as AI boosters insist, miracle drugs and endless vacations aren't far off … perhaps along with existential crises. Katharine Trendacosta, director of policy and advocacy at the Electronic Frontier Foundation, told The Register in an email that the EFF is glad to see state officials taking action against AI companies taking unreasonable risks with public safety. "Several recent cybersecurity incidents at AI labs could have been prevented or substantially mitigated by adhering to longstanding cybersecurity best practices, such as proper sandboxing, monitoring, and logging," said Trendacosta. "AI agents can be useful tools when deployed appropriately, with adequate safeguards designed to mitigate the risks. Companies should carefully consider the risks of every use case, including the consequences, reversibility, and sensitivity of any action an agent is used for." ®

articles.title: iPhone Duo Orders Will Now Arrive Before the Holidays
articles.content: Supplies of the iPhone Duo are improving, and many people will be able to get Apple's foldable before the holidays. New ‌iPhone Duo‌ orders placed today in the U.S. will arrive between December 16 and December 23, up from the prior January 25 delivery estimate. The December timing is available for all ‌iPhone Duo‌ colors and capacities. ‌iPhone Duo‌ orders were still listing a delivery date in January last Thursday, so the change was made in the last few days. Apple has been steadily improving iPhone Duo delivery dates for people who pre-ordered, and with new order dates moved up, all pre-orders should also arrive in December or earlier. We've heard reports from several users who originally had January delivery dates. Those orders have been moved to December 14 to December 21 in most cases, and some even earlier. During Apple's fourth-quarter earnings call, CEO John Ternus said Apple was working hard to get the Duo to as many customers as quickly as possible, but he had no timeline for when the company expected to reach supply/demand balance. articles.title: Hands-On With the iPhone Duo's New Face Unlock
articles.content: With iOS 27.3 beta 2, Apple is partially solving a common iPhone Duo complaint. There's a new feature for unlocking the device with the front camera, which we've tested out. Subscribe to the MacRumors YouTube channel for more videos. Unlock with Front Camera is a new option in iOS 27.3. If you turn it on, you can quickly unlock the ‌iPhone Duo‌ when it's closed. It's a feature that only works at the Lock Screen when the Duo is closed, so you can't use it for authenticating Apple Pay purchases or inserting logins and passwords from the Passwords app. You also need to use Touch ID or a passcode for unlocking the ‌iPhone Duo‌ when it's unfolded. Face unlock can be turned on in the ‌Touch ID‌ & Passcode section of the Settings app, and it works fairly well when it's active. You aren't going to have much luck in a dark room because it's just using the standard front camera, but if the lighting is decent, you can unlock without ‌Touch ID‌. Apple also added a "Close to Lock" feature that locks the ‌iPhone Duo‌ when you close it instead of transferring content to the outer display. These features are in the latest developer beta and will be available to everyone when iOS 27.3 is released in December.
