articles.title: NVIDIA DGX Spark Developer Kit Turns a Desk Into a Supercomputing Lab
articles.content: At SC26, an annual supercomputing conference taking place this week in Chicago, NVIDIA is introducing the DGX Spark HPC Developer Kit for researchers, academics and developers. The kit is a four-node cluster of NVIDIA DGX Spark systems , each connected directly to its two neighbors in a ring, with an NVIDIA HPC SDK installation playbook coming soon. Researchers get a place at their desk to run multi-node scientific workloads, AI models and agents, instead of waiting for time on a shared GPU cluster. The kit puts the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip on researchers’ desks. A Supercomputing Lab on Any Desk The DGX Spark Developer Kit changes how researchers work. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 It scales from one system, or node, to four — linked directly to one another over NVIDIA ConnectX-7 networking, with no network switch to buy or set up. At four nodes, it provides 512GB of combined memory and 20TB of NVMe storage that provides researchers more capacity to distribute models and scientific workloads across the cluster. With NVFP4, researchers can deploy models with up to 700B parameters locally across the four DGX Spark clusters, such as DeepSeek V4.1. With that much power at the desk, researchers with a fixed compute and server allocation no longer have to wait in a queue for every job. Teams can develop and debug on their own, saving server hours for production runs and keeping unpublished results, and proprietary datasets on premises. The playbook for NVIDIA HPC SDK is coming soon, bringing GPU-accelerated C, C++ and Fortran compilers, libraries and message passing interface tools to the DGX Spark cluster — the same development tools used on NVIDIA-powered supercomputers. Teams can build and test scientific applications across four nodes, check how computation and data are distributed, and debug communication issues before scaling to larger systems. The kit brings scientific simulation and AI models and agents to the desktop, with demonstrated four-system workloads including LAMMPS with Kokkos for materials simulation and NAMD for molecular dynamics. The broader DGX Spark community has validated GROMACS for molecular dynamics, OpenFOAM for fluid dynamics, WRF for weather modeling and NVIDIA NIM microservices such as OpenFold3 and Boltz-2 for predicting biomolecular structures. Running on DGX Spark, new open dataset and post-training recipes for Nemotron 3.5 Super VL help researchers adapt the model for life sciences and chemistry, enabling secure scientific workflows on infrastructure organizations control. What Researchers Can Do With It The kit opens up new possibilities for researchers. Researchers can explore agent-assisted workflows that prepare simulation inputs, launch runs and summarize results, while the scientists validate the setup and conclusions. Researchers can also train AI models that approximate slow simulations, then use them to refine wing designs toward minimum drag. Before committing supercomputer time, a team can narrow a 10-million-cell simulation to the 50-500 dimensions that matter. Kvantify is using NVIDIA cuQuantum, and reports running tensor-network simulations of quantum-chemistry circuits with up to 70 qubits and 975 gates on a single DGX Spark, benchmarking circuits generated for penicillin ground-state energy calculations. CYRAN AI , an IIT Delhi spin-out, uses DGX Spark and its PixelFlux library to accelerate JPEG 2000 decoding for large satellite images, supporting local geospatial analysis. OpenFold shows how researchers can fine-tune OpenFold3 on NVIDIA DGX Spark to improve protein-ligand structure predictions for drug discovery. The Rubin Lab at IGI at University of California, Berkeley is using a DGX Spark and NVIDIA Evo 2 model to predict bacterial traits directly from genome sequences by comparing embeddings from genomic and protein language models against the classical baselines. With no 11-hour cluster queue times, results arrived 15x sooner on DGX Spark. The Hartwig Group…

articles.title: Robo-soldier startup backed by Eric Trump misses payroll, may collapse
articles.content: A humanoid robotics company backed and advised by President Donald Trump’s son, Eric Trump, has reportedly missed payroll and may be on the brink of collapse after a funding shortfall. The Silicon Valley startup, Foundation Future Industries, claims it is developing and testing robots for military roles on battlefields from Ukraine to Gaza. Foundation failed to pay employees for the payroll period ending on October 30, anonymous sources told CNBC . The startup’s staff is especially angry because Foundation’s co-founder and CEO, Sankaet Pathak , supposedly borrowed $4.6 million in company funds to buy a luxury home overlooking San Francisco Bay about a year ago. This comes as Pathak and Foundation’s leadership are still looking to raise funding to support a $3 billion valuation, based on their promise to develop a humanoid robot ready for combat duty and capable of wielding various weapons. articles.title: macOS 27.3 beta 2 lets you limit what AI automation apps can see and do
articles.content: Full Disk Access in Apple's macOS 27.3 gives users tools to clamp down on what AI automation tools can access. Here's what's restricted. macOS 27.3 beta 2 adds granular options for AI automation apps and for apps that use Full Disk Access. On Monday, weeks after the arrival of the PROLED MacBook Pro , Apple made macOS 27.3 developer beta 2 available for download. The software aims to improve user safety and data protection through changes to system settings regarding third-party apps. The previous Device Control and Data Access option has been split into two settings: System & App Protection Override , and Accessibility . The former handles permissions for assistive apps by using entitlements, while the latter offers settings for apps that enable automation. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums

Apple often borrows ideas from Android, but the same is true the other way around. For example, Android Authority recently reported that Google has been working on bringing games to the Messages app , similar to the gaming experience in iMessage . At the time, there were no clues on how this feature would work. Now, we can answer some of those questions, thanks to some newly discovered information. The new details come from strings of code we spotted while diving into the latest beta (version messages.android_20261113_00_RC00.phone.openbeta_dynamic) of Google Messages. Internally known as “Midnight,” this feature will allow you to play games like pool, chess, checkers, darts, and more. One of the first new strings we came across specifically mentions you’ll be able to play nine classic games without having to leave the conversation.

articles.title: Build memory-aware AI agents with Agentic Retrieve on Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base
articles.content: Users of a knowledge-grounded application expect it to remember them, not only to search well. They ask follow-up questions that make sense only in the context of the previous turn. They expect an answer about a policy or a procedure to reflect what they told the application about themselves last month. And they still expect every answer to be grounded in the documents they are allowed to read, with citations. Whether the application is a customer support assistant, a document chat inside a SaaS product, or an internal assistant over company policies, the expectation is the same. Meeting that expectation is hard, because the context that would sharpen a search lives outside the knowledge base. A user’s location, role, or product tier was often mentioned in an unrelated conversation weeks ago. To use it, the application has to store every conversation, extract durable facts from it, decide which facts matter for the current question, and inject them into the request. When many users share the application, every one of those steps also has to be isolated per user, and so does every document. Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore , now take over these steps: storing each conversation, extracting facts from it, and bringing the relevant facts into the search. You turn this on by adding a memoryConfiguration to the AgenticRetrieveStream request, which makes AgentCore memory a retrieval source alongside your knowledge base. Within the same call, the service restores the conversation, and the planner decides on its own when a fact about the user would help. It retrieves that fact from long-term memory and uses it to compose the sub-queries it sends to the knowledge base. After generating the answer, the service saves the turn back to memory. The same request carries a userContext , so the knowledge base returns only the documents that the user’s access control lists (ACLs) allow. The integration is opt-in and backward compatible. Your application keeps only what is genuinely yours: authenticating the user and passing who they are. This post shows how to build such an assistant for many users who share one knowledge base and one memory resource. Each user sees only the documents they may read, and each user’s memory stays private. The running example is an internal employee assistant for AnyCompany, a fictional company. Employees sign in with Amazon Cognito and ask questions over HR policies, IT guides, engineering runbooks, and sales plans. We show how to read the user’s identity from the Cognito ID token, how to pass it to AgenticRetrieveStream for document ACLs and for memory, how to design memory namespaces for many users, and how to read the trace to see when the planner used memory. Finally, we make AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) enforce per-user memory isolation even when application code gets it wrong. If you deployed the application from Build multi-tenant agentic chat applications on enterprise data with Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base , this post replaces its “persist conversation history yourself” step. Solution overview AnyCompany keeps its documents in Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3). One managed knowledge base syncs them through an ACL-enabled Amazon S3 data source. A global ACL file in the same bucket says which employees may read each folder: everyone reads HR and IT, only engineers read the engineering runbooks, and only salespeople read the commission plan. One AgentCore memory resource is shared by every employee. Amazon Cognito authenticates employees, and its ID token supplies two claims: the sub (user ID) identifies the user’s memory, and the verified email identifies the user to the knowledge base’s ACL filter. Three test users sign in: two engineers, Maya and Liam, and one salesperson, Sofia. The trace excerpts in this post are taken from a run of the sample application in the GitHub repository . articles.title: Apple Plans to Release These 18 New Products Next Year
articles.content: Following a jam-packed couple of months in which it unveiled the iPhone Duo, HomeView, MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display, and so much more, Apple has likely cleared through its slate of remaining major product announcements this year. As always, the holiday season should be a relatively quiet time for Apple, and then things will pick back up again in 2027. Already, the company is expected to release at least 18 new products next year, including 20th-anniversary iPhone 20 Pro and iPhone 20 Pro Max models, all-new smart glasses, a larger HomeView, AirPods Pro with cameras, and more. Below, we have outlined new Apple products that are rumored to launch in 2027, according to Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman and rumors from other sources. iPhone iPhone 18e: A20 chip, 9GB of RAM, and longer battery life. iPhone 18: A20 chip, 9GB of RAM, and longer battery life. iPhone Air 2: A20 Pro chip, Ultra Wide camera, a smaller Dynamic Island, longer battery life, and Apple's C2 modem with mmWave support in the U.S. and "meaningfully faster" upload speeds compared to the current model's C1X modem. iPhone 20 Pro: A21 Pro chip and new design with "curved glass around all corners and edges" and thinner bezels around the screen. iPhone 20 Pro Max: A21 Pro chip and new design with "curved glass around all corners and edges" and thinner bezels around the screen. iPhone Duo 2: Face ID has apparently been tested, but it is unclear if the feature will be finalized in time for the iPhone Duo 2. And based on a recent rumor, the Camera Control button could eventually double as an Action button. iPad iPad Pro: M6 chip or M7 chip and a vapor chamber cooling system. iPad Air: M5 chip, OLED display, thinner and lighter design, and potentially the Acoustic Display feature that debuted on the iPad mini. iPad: A19 chip with Apple Intelligence support, N1 chip with Wi-Fi 7 support, and Apple's power-efficient C1X modem in cellular models. Apple Watch Apple Watch Series 13: A leaker claimed the Apple Watch will be receiving a major redesign next year, and this will apparently include a new way of attaching bands. If so, the Apple Watch Series 13 could have significant changes. Apple Watch Ultra 5: While an Apple Watch Ultra 5 has yet to be firmly rumored, a new Ultra model has arrived in four out of the past five years. Mac MacBook Neo: A19 Pro chip, 12GB of RAM, and potentially new color options. MacBook Air: M6 chip. MacBook Pro: An updated 14-inch MacBook Pro base model with an M7 chip and potentially a Dynamic Island and an illuminated Apple logo. MacBook Pro (PROLED XDR): M7 Pro and M7 Max chips. Other AirPods Pro: Built-in cameras for Siri AI and Visual Intelligence. Apple Glasses: iPhone-connected smart glasses with cameras, microphones, and speakers. Software features: Siri AI, Visual Intelligence, calling and messaging, notification announcements, music playback, and more. Apple is apparently targeting a WWDC 2027 unveiling and late 2027 availability. HomeView Max: A larger HomeView with a 9-inch screen that can swivel a full 360 degrees on a robotic arm. In the U.S., pricing may start at $999. Of course, these are only the products rumored so far, with 2027 likely to have more in store. This article, " Apple Plans to Release These 18 New Products Next Year " first appeared on MacRumors.com Discuss this article in our forums

articles.title: 15 retro tech gift ideas for the nostalgic gamer or builder in your life
articles.content: Technology has changed rapidly over the last few decades. While we've got hardware that's so much more powerful than what came 10 or 20 years ago, there's still a lot of enjoyment to be had in the classics. That's why there's a huge market for retro hardware, from game controllers designed to look like classic gamepads from old consoles, to full re-releases of old machines, with plenty of fun (and well-priced) accessories in between. If you're buying for a retro aficionado, you're going to want to pick up something that's fun to use and has a serious nostalgic edge. There's a whole host of gear out there for those who prefer an '80s or '90s aesthetic, rather than the products we live with today. ● Check out all these retro PC gift ideas on Amazon You can relive the glory days of yesteryear today with these retro gift ideas. We've put together some of the best ideas for a wistful techie who can upgrade their setup, with old-school designs ready for today's hardware. Check out the options we've hand-picked for you below. 40th Anniversary NEOGEO MINI Arcade Console: $59.99 This miniature recreation of a classic NeoGeo arcade cabinet includes 40 games (the average price of a Neo Geo game in the 1990s was $200, $8000 for all 40 games!) and includes classics like Metal Slug, The King of Fighters and of course, Fatal Fury . The console has scaled versions of the original controls, a 3.5-inch screen, and runs from a USB-C power supply. Need a bigger screen? You can connect via HDMI. External controllers and NeoGeo Mini Game controllers (available separately) can be used to retro game from the sofa! View Deal Thumby: $29.95 This Game Boy-style console is tiny (0.7 x 0.3 x 1.2 inches!) and is powered by the Raspberry Pi Pico's RP2040 microcontroller. Programmable via a web interface, you can make your own games and demos to share with others. View Deal Retro Cube 2 Speaker: $49.99 This gorgeous, retro-inspired N Edition Retro Cube 2 wireless speaker from 8BitDo offers stereo sound, with support for 2.4 GHz and Bluetooth connectivity, along with USB for wired use, and includes a wireless charging dock. View Deal A 1:1 scale replica of the gaming handheld that dominated the 1990s. This is a glorious piece of retro tech, preserved in Lego form for your shelves. Nintendo's Game Boy is an iconic piece of tech, and this Lego model is a replica of the great handheld. It comes with two cartridges, Super Mario Land and The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening. The screen can be replaced with a lenticular screen that recreates the original console's pixels. View Deal 3.5-inch IPS monitor with USB hub and SD card reader: $99.99 This retro Hagibis display comes with a 3.5-inch IPS LCD with a native resolution of 960 x 640, although it can scale up to 2,560 x 1,600 if you like punishing your eyes. It also includes several USB-A and USB-C ports with Gen 3.1 speeds, an HDMI port, as well as SD and TF card readers. View Deal X3 Mini PC: $638.99 This mini PC is retro-inspired, with a shell very reminiscent of the original NES. This is a fully-fledged PC, however, with an AMD Ryzen 7 H 255 CPU and integrated Radeon 780M GPU, along with 16GB RAM and a 1TB SSD. View Deal 87 Keys Retro Mechanical Keyboard - N Edition: $99.99 This fun retro-inspired keyboard from 8Bitdo looks like a favored NES console from the good old days. It comes with a set of dual giant buttons, which is similar to a Nintendo controller style. It has multi-function connectivity and a unique look that's perfect for a gaming enthusiast. It also comes with two separate 'super buttons' that you can map to keys or macros. View Deal MiniToo Retro PC-Style Computer Speaker, Smart Pixel Screen: $59.99 It looks like a retro computer, but this is actually a 90s-inspired 1.77-inch mini Bluetooth speaker with a smart pixel screen, an alarm clock, and focus tools. articles.title: China retains fastest supercomputer in the world crown as AI data centers soak up new hardware
articles.content: China's LineShine remains the world's highest-performing supercomputer, according to the 68 th edition of the Top500 list published at SC26 in Chicago on Monday. For the first time in decades, the supercomputer ranking saw exceptionally few additions despite unprecedented demand for high-performance computing hardware, as the vast amounts of compute resources deployed these days are destined for artificial intelligence (AI) data centers rather than traditional supercomputers. Top 10 supercomputers unchanged China's LineShine , installed at the National Supercomputer Center in Shenzhen, offers sustained FP64 compute performance of 2.198 FP64 ExaFLOPS in the High Performance Linpack (HPL) benchmark at 42.22 MW. The machine relies on the homegrown LingKun platform with 304-core Armx9-based LX2 processors clocked at 1.55 GHz (13,789,440 cores in total) and the proprietary LingQi interconnect. Unlike the other four exascale-class supercomputers, LineShine does not use any compute accelerators and exclusively relies on CPUs, which is largely why it only gains 3.6X performance when moving from FP64 to mixed-precision data, which is lower than systems that use low-precision accelerators. (Image credit: Top 500) America's most powerful El Capitan supercomputer at the Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory relies on AMD's Instinct MI300A accelerated processing units (APUs), and the HPE Cray EX255a platform delivers 1.809 FP64 ExaFLOPS at 29.69 MW, which makes it significantly more power-efficient than its rival from China. The Frontier supercomputer at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory, based on AMD's 3 rd Generation EPYC processors and Instinct MI250X compute GPUs, achieves 1.353 FP64 ExaFLOPS at 24.61 MW. Meanwhile, Aurora at the Argonne National Laboratory, which uses Intel's Xeon CPU Max 9470 processors and Data Center GPU Max accelerators, offers 1.012 FP64 ExaFLOPS at 38.70 MW. All three American exascale supercomputers use HPE’s Cray EX platforms and Slingshot-11 interconnect. Germany’s Jupiter Booster at the Jülich Supercomputing Center, which employs Nvidia’s GH200 Grace Hopper Superchips, the BullSequana XH3000 platform, and Nvidia’s quad-rail InfiniBand NDR200 interconnect, delivers 1.0 FP64 ExaFLOPS at 15.79 MW and remains the most energy-efficient exascale supercomputer on the list. Remarkably, neither the 10 highest-performing supercomputers nor the 10 most energy-efficient machines have changed their positions since June. Only 27 new supercomputers in Top 500 Only 27 new supercomputers (5.4% of all machines on the list) made it to the November edition of the Top 500, the lowest number since the project was founded in 1993. The most powerful newcomer is South Korea's Hanggang at the KISTI Supercomputing Center, which occupies the 12 th position with 342.6 FP64 PFLOPS. The machine uses Nvidia's GH200 Grace Hopper Superchips and HPE's Cray EX254n platform. Hanggang also ranks eighth in the HPCG benchmark with 4.29 HPCG PFLOPS. The aggregate HPL performance of the world's 500 highest-performing supercomputers increased by a modest 4.4% over the past six months to 19.57 FP64 ExaFLOPS. Nonetheless, it now takes a machine with 2.857 PFLOPS of sustained FP64 performance to qualify for the TOP500, up 7.3% from 2.662 PFLOPS in June. The performance of the systems ranked 50 th and 100 th rose from 49.85 PFLOPS to 55.81 PFLOPS (12%) and from 21.85 PFLOPS to 22.74 PFLOPS, respectively. Also, there are now 27 machines that deliver at least 100 PFLOPS of FP64 performance, up from 25 in June, whereas the number of supercomputers equipped with compute accelerators increased from 275 to 291 (58.2%). Everything goes to AI data centers The historically low number of new entrants to the Top 500 is particularly noteworthy given the unprecedented scale of investments in advanced computing infrastructure these days. articles.title: AI agents were all over KubeCon. Production is another story
articles.content: AI agents are testing systems that were originally built for people, and Jonathan Bryce thinks the cloud-native community has a lot of work to do to help those systems keep up in this new era. The New Stack sat down with Bryce, the executive director of the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America in Salt Lake City to talk about the projects joining the foundation and how AI is changing its work. Bryce tells The New Stack , “A lot of the existing systems in our world were built for human speed, and agent speed is a completely different type of usage pattern and scenario, and so these systems are just not scalable and resilient enough to handle the kind of workloads that agents are generating.” Running training and inference workloads on Kubernetes is already a familiar job for this community, and Bryce argues that the financial services, healthcare, and transportation systems that agents interact with will also need the elasticity and observability that cloud-native technologies provide. OpenShell and Agent Substrate At KubeCon, Nvidia announced that it was contributing OpenShell to the CNCF . Google had also announced the donation of Agent Substrate ahead of the show. Both joined the CNCF as Sandbox projects, the foundation’s entry-level tier. At its core, OpenShell enforces policies, including which files, networks, credentials, and model endpoints an agent can access. Agent Substrate tackles a related but different issue by providing isolated environments for agents on Kubernetes, with features like support for suspending idle sessions and resuming them when needed. “We can make AI systems that have security and control architected into them from the infrastructure side,” Bryce says. He sees this as a responsibility for the community, given the questions AI has raised about security and resource consumption. Moving a project like OpenShell into neutral governance also lets more companies contribute to it, he says. Doing more with existing hardware Agent workloads also aren’t as evenly distributed as those of more traditional enterprise applications. “Your agent, even if it’s always waiting around to be at your beck and call, it’s not necessarily doing work 24/7,” Bryce says. “How do you spin it down and spin it up where it feels like it’s ready for you at any time? That’s going to be the user experience that people demand. How do you do that without just having it sit there and burn CPU cycles on nothing?” Agent Substrate saves the agent’s state and frees up the compute it was using, then restores the session onto an available worker. Bryce also highlighted llm-d , the distributed inference framework, as an example of software getting more out of existing hardware. While hardware is expensive, expensive to run, and (at least currently) in limited supply, software gives developers something they can work on now. A flood of vulnerability reports Zero-days and security also came up more at this KubeCon than in previous years. As more people use AI tools to find and report vulnerabilities, Bryce says, open source maintainers have been flooded with duplicate and unverified reports that they still have to take seriously. He thinks the pace may no longer be accelerating the way it was early this year, but he isn’t sure what 2027 will bring as the models keep getting better. “Y2K didn’t end up being that big of a deal,” he says. “This is really a moment that could be a big deal if we don’t actually just all get together and work as quickly as we can.” Agent adoption is still early For all the talk about agents at the show, though, Bryce’s assessment of adoption is measured. “Beyond software development, adoption is still quite low,” he says. articles.title: How Duco transforms financial data automation with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
articles.content: Financial institutions face a critical challenge: processing massive volumes of data with speed, accuracy, and compliance while operating under some of the world’s strictest regulatory frameworks. Duco is the agentic Operations platform for financial services, serving tier-one banks and other financial institutions. It processes 20 billion transactions monthly for 200+ clients, including 7 of the top 20 banks and 10 of the top 20 asset managers. To keep pace as data processing demands grew, Duco evolved from traditional machine learning models to the agentic AI capabilities of Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. In this post, we share how Duco rebuilt its agentic AI stack on these services, cutting deployment time and onboarding costs while keeping each bank’s data isolated. The challenge: Scaling intelligence in a regulated environment Duco’s platform empowers teams to automate mission-critical data processes using AI and no-code models, handling everything from data extraction to downstream publication. It already used traditional machine learning models for predictive labeling and pattern recognition, helping banks consolidate and automate over 20,000 processes. However, these classical machine learning approaches had inherent limitations. They required extensive historical data for training, struggled with novel scenarios, and demanded significant customization for each new use case. Most critically, they couldn’t adapt quickly to the diverse, constantly evolving data formats and business rules that characterize modern financial operations. “The classical prediction models worked to an extent, but they weren’t agile or flexible enough. Traditional machine learning models can only amplify what they’ve already learned — they can’t help with the next step or find new problems.” — Rob Gates, Chief Architect and Innovation Officer, Duco The solution: Amazon Bedrock and Bedrock AgentCore Duco made a strategic decision to adopt Amazon Bedrock for managed access to foundation models, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to run agents at scale. This was more than a technology upgrade. It was a fundamental shift in how its system could understand, reason about, and act on financial data. About Amazon Bedrock and Bedrock AgentCore Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed service that offers a choice of high-performing foundation models from leading AI companies through a single API, along with a broad set of capabilities to build generative AI applications with security, privacy, and responsible AI. Learn more about Amazon Bedrock . Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is the platform to build, connect, and optimize AI agents at scale. Build with any open source framework and any model. Connect agents to your tools and data with authentication and access controls built in. Monitor and improve agents in production with tracing and evaluation. AgentCore handles the infrastructure so you focus on agent logic, not backend plumbing, and you get enterprise security and reliability without giving up open source flexibility. Learn more on the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore product page. Why Amazon Bedrock? Several factors made Amazon Bedrock the ideal choice for Duco’s regulated financial services industry (FSI) environment: Security and compliance first: With Amazon Bedrock, customer data stays within the AWS environment, and it is not used to train models. With private endpoints in its virtual private cloud (VPC), Duco can connect to internal systems while keeping them completely isolated, which matters for sensitive financial data processing. Model flexibility: Access to leading foundation models from the Amazon Nova 2 family, Anthropic, OpenAI, Cohere, Meta, and Mistral AI through a single API means Duco can choose the right model for each task. Duco can switch between models by changing a configuration parameter. Built for financial services: Amazon Bedrock provides the robust governance controls and compliance frameworks that financial services require,…

articles.title: The FAA’s ground stop has a simple culprit. Its causes may not
articles.content: On Friday afternoon, L3Harris Technologies was doing what it has done at Federal Aviation Administration facilities month after month: moving a communications line off decades-old copper and onto fiber, work that federal auditors count as part of a $12.5 billion overhaul of the country’s air traffic control system. Shortly after a technician installed a new router at an FAA radio site in El Dorado, Arkansas, the device began pumping out data—so much that the flood disrupted communications at 17 of the 22 so-called en route centers that handle high-altitude traffic. At 3:36 p.m. Eastern, with about 3,500 planes in the air, the FAA held all departures nationwide. The stop lasted more than four hours, until 8:15 p.m. Airlines canceled more than 5,000 flights by Saturday and about 1,500 more on Sunday as they repositioned crews and aircraft. It was the first nationwide ground stop since January 2023, when the system that sends safety notices to pilots failed. “We haven’t determined what the fault was,” Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said at a Saturday news conference. Investigators are trying to establish whether L3Harris installed or configured the router incorrectly, or whether the equipment itself was at fault. Adam Bauer, a spokesperson for Hewlett Packard Enterprise, which owns router maker Juniper Networks, told Fast Company its devices appeared to have worked as intended. “Based on what we know and have been told by others, our equipment was working as configured.” But the failure exposed weaknesses the FAA has been warned about for years: a contractor that has run the FAA’s network since 2002 and has a record of outages, an integrator the agency’s own staff rated a financial risk, a technician workforce the FAA admits is understaffed, and a $12.5 billion overhaul that auditors say is racing ahead without a master schedule. There is no evidence yet that any of them caused Friday’s failure. Still, some critics see Friday’s chaos as years of warnings come true. “The sad fact is this has happened before,” Mary Schiavo, a former Transportation Department inspector general, told NPR’s Weekend Edition. The sprawling network of copper and fiber that carries the country’s air traffic communications across roughly 4,400 FAA sites still runs largely on technology that dates back decades. Some older equipment, including radar, requires replacement parts that can only be obtained through online auction websites or made with 3D printers. In 2023, an FAA-commissioned panel of outside experts warned that the condition of the agency’s facilities and equipment was “elevating system risk to unsustainable levels.” The agency under President Joe Biden had commissioned another group of aviation experts to examine air traffic control in October 2024, but weeks after Trump took office, the group learned it was being disbanded, The Washington Post reported . Last May, Duffy said the FAA was speeding up its overhaul of the system under a program called BNATCS, or the Brand New Air Traffic Control System. Congress approved $12.5 billion for the effort, which aims to modernize the telecom network by the end of 2028, before the end of Trump’s term, and 21 months ahead of an earlier September 2030 target. In September, the Government Accountability Office released its latest report on the overhaul. The FAA was moving at an unprecedented speed, auditors said, but without a reliable lifecycle cost estimate or an integrated master schedule. Instead, auditors counted 11,389 separate project schedules that had not been coordinated, so different programs were booked to visit the same sites repeatedly or in ways that risk “excessive disruptions to air traffic control operations” and could jeopardize the FAA’s “aggressive deployment schedule.” Delays, in turn, could leave controllers reliant on outdated systems that are prone to failure, and “lead to more system outages,…

articles.title: FBI Says Artex AI Open-Source Hacking Tool Used to Breach Networks In 'Under Three Hours'
articles.content: The FBI is warning (PDF) that hackers are using the AI-powered penetration-testing tool Artex to compromise networks in "under three hours" in some cases. The tool has been linked to attacks against South Korean financial institutions, at least 2,250 ConnectWise customers and Barracuda. TechCrunch reports: Artex is one of several open-source AI-powered penetration testing platforms, a category of software built to probe a network's defenses. Hackers can connect Artex to hosted frontier large language models (LLMs) like those from Anthropic and OpenAI, as well as to open-source models and non-U.S. models. The FBI says Artex intrusions can be "noisy," meaning they generate reams of traffic and data that may trigger a targeted company's defensive alerts. But the tools allow hackers to move at speeds that makes it far more harder for human defenders to keep up. In some cases, Artex-linked attacks can move from targeting a system to active compromise "in under three hours." Oftentimes, Artex will rely on rapidly scanning a victim's network to look for signs of weakness, and then exploit simple security bugs, such as weak protections and exposed or stolen passwords to gain a foothold. From there, Artex allows the hacker to spread across the network for databases, mailboxes, and other sensitive information. [...] After Artex was used in cyberattacks, the tool's developer made the software closed-source to prevent further attacks. But the FBI says the previous open-source version continues to circulate and remains "widely accessible" for use in cyberattacks. It's not only companies and targeted victims that have been compromised as a result of weakened security exploited by AI tools; the tools themselves have been exposed as well, potentially allowing outsiders to access powerful hacking capabilities. Last week, researchers found hundreds of publicly exposed Artex systems online, which had been placed on the internet without a password, likely by mistake or misconfiguration -- including the Artex system that was used to target South Korea. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Apple's face unlock for iPhone Duo works well, avoids Android's issues
articles.content: The main complaint about iPhone Duo is the lack of Face ID and the convenience it offers, so Apple has introduced a less secure face recognition option that can't be tricked with a photo. iPhone Duo can now be unlocked using the front-facing outer camera When Apple introduced Face ID , it showed off how even complex Hollywood masks couldn't fool the system thanks to proof-of-life algorithms. Android smartphones have offered face recognition for years, but many were easily fooled by a 2D photograph. Thanks to the highly insecure nature of face recognition that doesn't rely on infrared dot scattering and 3D mapping, it seemed Apple would never implement it. Then, as it started pushing for more advanced systems powered by Secure Exclaves , the feature popped up in Apple HomeView and then was added to iPhone Duo. articles.title: Three small failures combined to take down Microsoft 365
articles.content: A hidden defect in Microsoft's cloud gateway, dormant since July, was to blame for one of the largest outages in the company's history last week. A preliminary Post-Incident Report (PIR) released by the company outlines how the latent bug, changes in traffic, and reduced server capacity combined to knock much of Microsoft 365 and Exchange infrastructure offline at the end of last week. Microsoft's report lists the incident's final status as "a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents." Microsoft's preliminary report places the outage between November 12 at 16:20 UTC and November 13 at 16:10 UTC, just under 24 hours total, and additional monitoring remained in place for any affected systems through November 14. The outage started on November 12 and quickly rippled through businesses and public offices that depend on Microsoft's cloud and email exchange infrastructure. The outage is covered in Microsoft's incident IDs EX1550543 and MO1550821. You need Microsoft 365 admin credentials to see the full report on the company's status pages, but Office Watch has reproduced the preliminary report , and the University of Pennsylvania maintains an archive of Microsoft's service-health updates . Read full article Comments

articles.title: Taxonomy of multi-agent design patterns, anti-patterns, and lessons from manufacturing
articles.content: Enterprise teams are building multi-agent systems, and when early implementations fall short, the cause is rarely the model. Multi-agent coordination is a distributed systems problem, and many teams taking it on haven’t yet built distributed systems instincts. The numbers are consistent across sources: ~88% of AI pilots never reach production . Stanford HAI demonstrated that two models can perform worse collaborating than either alone when coordination overhead exceeds the benefit. The pattern is clear: teams are adding complexity faster than they build understanding. Ten steps that are each 95 percent reliable deliver only 59.9 percent end-to-end reliability, and 20 steps deliver 35.8 percent. This illustrative model assumes a strictly sequential chain with no retries, but the direction holds: each dependent handoff multiplies risk. In this post, you learn how to decide whether a use case needs multiple agents, choose a coordination pattern, and spot costly anti-patterns early. You also see how takt time, safety boundaries, edge data, and shift cycles shape the architecture. Multi-agent coordination patterns Coordination patterns fall into two tiers, based on who controls the flow. In Tier 1, you define the path. In Tier 2, the model chooses the path at runtime. That flexibility handles work whose steps you can’t define in advance, at a higher cost in tokens, latency, and debugging. The practical default is to start with Tier 1 and move a task to Tier 2 only when its subtasks emerge during the work. Tier 1: Patterns (deterministic control flow) 1.1 Sequential Pipeline: Orchestration patterns that implement linear execution where each node’s output feeds into the next node (A -> B -> C) supporting ordered processing with predictable execution timing In the following diagram, input flows to agent A (extract), then agent B (transform), then agent C (validate), and then output. The user defines that order at build time, and nothing is decided at runtime. As a result, the pipeline is straightforward to debug and test, and its cost is predictable. Typical fits include document processing, extract, transform, and load (ETL) chains, and warranty-claim triage. Figure 1: Sequential pipeline where each agent’s output feeds the next, from extract to transform to validate 1.2 Conditional Workflow: Logic-based edges select the next node by condition, so the workflow can branch and send each case down a different path. In the following diagram, a user request goes to agent A (write code) and then to agent B (test code). A pass/fail check sends passing work to agent D (deploy). Failing work loops back to agent A for a retry, up to a maximum of N times, and then escalates to a human. The orchestration layer enforces that cap, for example through an AWS Step Functions iteration limit, which keeps the loop from becoming the unbounded iteration anti-pattern described later in this post. Figure 2: Conditional workflow that retries failures up to N times before escalating to a human 1.3 Conditional Router : A classification step examines the input and directs it to the appropriate processing path. Only one path is executed per request. Best for intent-driven dispatch, quality-gate decisions, customer inquiry routing, and anomaly triage. The following diagram shows a plant supervisor’s request being read by a classifier and sent to exactly one specialist. Questions about whether parts meet spec go to the Quality Agent, overdue equipment services go to the Maintenance Agent, and shift changes go to the Scheduling Agent. This decision is made at the entry point. Figure 3: Conditional router that runs one path per request, with bounded retries before human escalation 1.4 Parallel Workflow: A task splits into independent subtasks that run simultaneously across handlers, each on its own data. A fan-in step combines the results when all handlers complete, and a failure in one path retries only that path. Best for multi-source analysis, batch processing,…

articles.title: Infoblox customer and staff data exposed in Sharepoint breach
articles.content: Networking and security firm Infoblox is investigating a third-party breach that allowed crims to access sensitive customer and staff data. "Infoblox is investigating a security event involving unauthorized access to certain company information through a compromised third-party data migration vendor,” a company spokesperson confirmed to The Register . According to sources, the compromised third-party data migration vendor had trusted access to Infoblox's SharePoint system, and the intruders used this vendor’s accounts and access to exfiltrate data directly from Microsoft SharePoint. This data included configuration information related to some customer's NIOS (Network Identity Operating System) deployments. These are saved snapshots of customers’ network data, such as DNS, DHCP configurations, Grid databases, and reporting logs, that can be used to fully recover the appliance or grid in case of a system failure or faulty upgrade. The intruders also stole employee data during the break-in. According to an email CEO Scott Harrell sent to employees, which The Register has seen, compromised employee details include financial information such as direct deposit details, contact info, dates of birth, and Social Security numbers for employees and dependents. Upon discovering the breach, Infoblox “immediately activated” its incident response procedures, and took steps to contain the incident, including hiring outside cybersecurity experts, the spokesperson said. “We have sent notifications about this security event and are providing support and guidance as appropriate,” the Infoblox spokesperson told us. “Based on our investigation to date, we have no indication that any Infoblox products, cloud services, software updates or build-and-release processes were involved. Our priority is to fully investigate and resolve this issue." Affected staff received a $100 "spot bonus" to buy password management services, and were warned to be "especially alert for phishing, vishing, fraud, or other suspicious communications." Infoblox also gave employees and their dependents free credit monitoring and identity protection for two years. Infoblox declined to answer our more detailed questions about the compromise, including the type of data exposed, and how many employees and customers might be affected. The Register will update this story as we learn more about the breach.®

articles.title: New US rules aim to restrict Chinese firms’ remote access to AI servers and infrastructure
articles.content: New steps have been taken to ensure that countries and companies that are not on whitelists that would allow them to import advanced AI hardware cannot use cloud-based workarounds. The U.S. Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has today unveiled an interim final rule, or IFR, in collaboration with the Department of Treasury and the National Security Council, aimed at backing up existing limitations on the export of hardware built by companies like Nvidia to non-whitelisted companies based in countries such as China. "The rule is designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements" using data centers in third-party countries, a statement explains. Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc) While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply market The state of China's decade-long semiconductor push Huawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fab China's latest round of rare-earth export controls explained Nvidia, for example, is only allowed to export its high-performance AI chips to companies that are on a whitelist. But amid ongoing claims of black market GPU sales and a recent crackdown on overseas AI GPU rentals from China , it has become clear that these restrictions perhaps aren't as robust as they were intended to be. Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs were even recently discovered in a data center used by China Telecom . But while blocking the sale of physical goods is one thing, the cloud-based workaround is another entirely. Nvidia itself told data center operators earlier this month that they must limit remote access to their services — 51% of their business must come from non-Chinese companies. But, again, it's unclear how effective that approach has been in ensuring access to powerful AI capabilities doesn't fall into the wrong hands, even if they're accessed remotely rather than in person. The new BIS rule means that overseas data centers will be required to do more to limit access to their services where U.S-based technology is being used. Restrictions will also be placed on data centers that supply remote access to companies whose headquarters are deemed to be in higher-risk countries, such as China, Russia, and Iran. A license will also be required for anyone trying to export advanced chips to companies with headquarters in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil. The new requirements will officially go into effect in 90 days. This latest rule comes against a backdrop of ongoing uncertainty over America's AI crown jewel, Nvidia. Jensen Huang, the company's CEO, resigned after confirming an affair , but is now potentially in line for a quick-fire comeback, despite the fact that the woman involved in the affair is an alleged Chinese spy .
articles.author: Oliver Haslam

articles.title: Researchers ‘recognize that AI will never replace HPC,’ says AMD executive — high-precision workloads will ‘exist for a very long time’ even as AI usage expands
articles.content: While AI continues to reshape industries across science and mathematics, traditional supercomputing has seemingly taken a back seat. However, AMD's Scott Tease told Tom's Hardware Premium that most HPC sites “recognize that AI will never replace HPC,” and suggests that building a heterogeneous compute stack is the best path forward to tackle bleeding-edge research, despite Nvidia pushing performance on lower-precision data types higher for AI workloads at the cost of native performance for the important double-precision FP64 format that’s critical for HPC workloads. A heterogeneous compute stack brings together quantum, HPC, and AI under one roof, a fleet that AMD is helping pilot at Oak Ridge National Laboratory alongside IBM. Tease is AMD’s corporate vice president of HPC and sovereign AI, who joined the company earlier this year after more than a decade at Lenovo (and, before that, another 13 years at IBM). We spoke with Tease ahead of SC26 to get a read on the state of HPC, how it intersects with AI, and what’s actually driving the research community in a time when computer chips are driving headlines about international espionage plots. An awful lot of numbers (Image credit: AMD) FP64 is important for HPC workloads because of its precision. FP64 is a hot-button issue, largely due to how Nvidia’s GPUs have progressed over the past two generations. Or rather, how they haven't progressed. Nvidia’s latest Rubin GPU has 33 TFLOPs of FP64 compute, which is lower than the four-year-old H100’s 34 TFLOPs of FP64. For context, AMD’s year-old Instinct MI355X peaks at 78.6 TFLOPs of FP64 compute, while its upcoming HPC-angled MI430X peaks at 288 TFLOPs. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Nvidia has leaned on emulation to drive FP64 performance higher, a tactic that AMD is now pushing back on , but regardless, it’s easy to see why the HPC world could feel left behind in this new AI era. AI is defined by fuzzy, low-precision data formats, which is diametrically opposed to the accuracy of high-precision FP64. And, over the last generations of hardware from the big green giant that is Nvidia, FP64 performance has seemingly stalled in favor of driving low-precision data formats for AI workloads. “Maybe a few years ago, people in HPC might have felt a little threatened by AI because it was taking some of the limelight,” Tease told Tom’s Hardware Premium. “But I think now they’ve come to realize that AI is an essential part of scientific discovery today. It’s just, how are you going to deploy it?” That central question recontextualizes the apparent conflict between AI compute and HPC compute. Tease pointed to researchers spawning dozens of agents to explore viable paths for a given intent, while still leaving the complex simulations for a traditional FP64-driven HPC fleet. “...to try to do that with old approaches where you have islands of CPUs or islands of GPUs or something like that, and they're very different. They're not interconnected. It's just not going to be able to keep up,” Tease said. Enter quantum (Image credit: IBM) One of the challenges right now is actually connecting those systems, which is an area AMD is exploring with its recent collaboration with IBM and Oak Ridge National Laboratory to deploy AMD’s “classical” computing stack in the Umbra HPC system alongside IBM’s 129-qubit Quantum Nighthawk quantum computer. The systems will connect to the Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility, allowing researchers to “explore how integrated quantum, AI, and scientific computing can accelerate scientific discoveries and national security.” If the HPC crowd felt slighted by AI, you can imagine how quantum researchers probably feel. Regardless, Tease says the future of scientific computing looks like a unified fleet that brings together AI, HPC, and quantum. “There [are] going to be a lot of problems where quantum will not be the be-all, end-all. There are some problems like human health, chemistry, where quantum’s going to allow us to…

articles.title: Google found hackers using autonomous AI agents to turn security patches into exploits
articles.content: Google’s Threat Intelligence Group says attackers are using autonomous AI agents to reverse-engineer security patches, generate exploits, and attempt to execute them without human approval. In a report published Monday , Google and Mandiant describe the first cases their researchers have identified of attackers using LLM frameworks to fully automate vulnerability discovery and exploitation. The framework uses an orchestrator to coordinate specialized agents, share context, and invoke tools through interfaces such as MCP. The agents apply familiar coding workflows to offensive security, identifying vulnerabilities, generating exploit candidates, and testing them against targets. Inside the exploit pipeline Google found a publicly exposed staging server running a multi-agent framework called exploit_agent alongside stolen victim data and scripts used after a successful intrusion. The framework connected several frontier and locally hosted language models to automate patch diffing, turning potential vulnerabilities into exploit code that it could then attempt to execute. The server also contained scripts for reconnaissance, brute-force attacks, installing webshells, and removing those left by competing attackers. Google found evidence that the operators were interested in French media, entertainment, and education websites, and that the framework had examined access controls in the Spectra WordPress plugin. What’s changed is that agents can now do much of that work themselves. Patch diffing is nothing new. Attackers have been comparing code before and after security patches for years to figure out what was fixed and how to exploit it. What’s changed is that agents can now do much of that work themselves. Google didn’t identify which models handled individual tasks or disclose how often the generated exploits succeeded. And while the server contained stolen data, researchers couldn’t determine whether exploit_agent obtained it. Agent harnesses go offensive Google also found attackers using open-source offensive frameworks built around orchestration patterns familiar from coding agents . CAIRN coordinates specialized agents through a shared blackboard and an observe-orient-decide-act loop, using the results of each task to determine what happens next. Google observed the framework in intrusions targeting U.S. aerospace organizations. Other frameworks take different approaches. CyberStrikeAI uses a Go backend to orchestrate commercial and open-weight models across more than 100 security tools, YAML attack recipes, and custom scripts. HexStrike AI exposes more than 150 offensive security tools through MCP , with specialized agents handling reconnaissance, exploitation and binary analysis. Faster than patch cycles Publicly available vulnerability information is also reaching attackers faster, leaving defenders less time to deploy fixes . After two PaperCut vulnerabilities were exploited as zero-days in August, security researchers and Huntress developed working exploits with LLM assistance within a day of disclosure. The attacker moved from initial access to domain administrator within minutes. GreyNoise documented a campaign four days after the initial disclosure in which an attacker likely used language models to develop exploits, build target lists, and attack hundreds of organizations. The attacker moved from initial access to domain administrator within minutes. Two PHP vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, presented a similar risk when patched code and a proof-of-concept video became public ahead of the official October 21 release. Hundreds of purported exploits appeared online after the patches shipped, although many didn’t work and were likely generated with LLM assistance. Security teams then had to determine which exploits posed a real threat and which were simply nonfunctional code. Velocity over stealth These frameworks are still relatively easy to detect. articles.title: Crypto ETFs: Bringing Centralization Back to Crypto?
articles.content: The whole point of cryptocurrencies is to offer a decentralized alternative to traditional financial infrastructure with middlemen. In this way, costs and risks, such as blockages and censorship, are reduced. And yet, here we are again, with digital assets reentering the traditional financial world in the form of Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs). An ETF is an investment vehicle whose shares trade on a stock exchange. In other words, it’s an asset that represents something else without direct exposure —in this case, cryptocurrencies . Spot products hold the underlying crypto, while futures products use contracts linked to its price. So far, coins like Bitcoin (BTC), Ether (ETH), and Ripple (XRP) have their own ETF products available for investors. There’s a lot of money in there, too. According to CoinStats , crypto ETFs have over $171 billion of Assets Under Management (AUM). Such a fact begs the question: is this really beneficial for the want-to-be decentralized crypto world, or is it just a blatant invasion from the old financial system? Let’s explore this topic. ETFs Are Not Crypto The first thing we must consider is that crypto-related ETFs are not cryptocurrency themselves, in any way, shape, or form. Instead, with a spot ETF, the investor owns shares in a financial product that holds the underlying asset. That means there’s a company (or another middleman) behind this product, handling all the real coins on your behalf —but you’ll never see the real coins themselves. Future-based products don’t even have third-party coins, and only obtain exposure through financial contracts. Investing in a crypto ETF isn’t the same as “owning” crypto. You’re basically buying a ticket that represents a certain amount of gold, but it’s not, and it’ll never be, the gold itself . The value of that ticket is completely out of your control, and the middleman who sells these tickets takes a nice cut for handling them. If we think about it in simple terms, that’s it, that’s a crypto ETF. Well, put that way, it sounds almost like a scam—though, of course, it isn't. There are many people, and especially institutions, that cannot or don’t wish to manage their own "gold" (their own cryptocurrencies). This investment vehicle is a service that offers them greater security and convenience, allowing them to gain some exposure without the major risks. After all, self-custody has its perils , too. What Crypto ETFs Can Improve Self-custody requires work and responsibility, while many investors are more familiar with the brokerage environment. They often rely on regulated middlemen to handle sensitive financial transactions, and they’re comfortable within this system. Big companies, especially, aren’t suddenly learning how to properly set up and store a cold wallet with millions of dollars inside. Instead, they’re hiring the services or buying the products of experts in the matter, if they want to add crypto to their portfolios. Therefore, trust is something ETFs can bring to the crypto world. And regulated trust is what institutions are usually looking for. Institutional participation can bring more liquidity (always a good thing) and connect crypto markets with traditional finance. The scale of recent inflows shows that these products have become an important bridge between the two worlds. As described by CoinStats, there was an inflow of over $5.2 billion to crypto ETFs in August alone. Regulated investment products like ETFs introduce disclosure, reporting, and oversight requirements that many crypto platforms have historically lacked, so that’s why institutions may prefer them over self-custody. Access can be easier too, since you can buy through a traditional brokerage account. Someone else is responsible for every difficult part, and you just handle your investment. It’s fast and not cheap, but convenient. That’s maybe the worst part. When Convenience Creates Concentration Convenience is not synonymous with security—not by a long shot. Exchanges can…

articles.title: macOS 27.3 Warns Against Giving AI Apps Full Mac Control
articles.content: With the latest macOS 27.3 beta, Apple is giving Mac users more control over the data they share and the access they give to apps, including apps that use AI agents. Apple today informed developers about upcoming changes to the Full Disk Access API and the Device Control and Data Access API. Here's what Apple says is changing : The current Device Control and Data Access setting will be split into two options that make it clearer to users what they're permitting. The setting is becoming System & App Protection Override and Accessibility. There will be a single method for granting permissions by selecting the app requesting access from a list. Apple will encourage users to grant access to just the specific apps (in System & App Protection Override) or folders (for Full Disk Access) required for workflows. Apple will better inform users about the data apps will receive access to or control over if full permissions are given. Users will have an option to configure apps to ask each time for required access rather than granting an app unrestricted access. There will be a transparency indicator when a requesting app is controlling another app with System & App Protection Override. The indicator will be displayed in the Mac menu bar. Apple says developers will need to adjust user onboarding and make sure apps can "gracefully handle" access to a limited set of folders or apps when using the APIs being overhauled. Apps that use Full Disk Access for disk backup or the new Accessibility settings for assistive technologies can request entitlements to offer the same experience for new installations that they offered before macOS 27.3. Right now, known apps keep their current experience without an entitlement, and app permissions granted by users prior to macOS 27.3 will remain in effect. Mac users will see these changes when approving new app permission requests, and entitlement details are coming soon. Last month, Apple said it would add "additional controls" for Full Disk Access on Macs because of the risks posed by AI agents. Apple warned that some developers are using Full Disk Access in ways that can put users at risk, exposing files, mail, messages, browsing history, and more. articles.title: AMD grabs over 40% of new TOP500 list for supercomputers, up 14% since last year
articles.content: With the coming of SC26, also comes a fresh edition of the TOP500 list, which ranks the world's most powerful supercomputers. The newly released list illustrates that AMD powers 40% of the list, up 14% compared to 2025. AMD-powered systems now tally up to 202 on the list, up from 177 last year. New to the list is Lux, a “SI + HPC supercomputer” developed by AMD and the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), which debuted at position 14. AMD’s representation in the top 10 is familiar. After debuting in June, China’s LineShine remains in the top slot. El Capitan, powered by AMD chips, is in the second slot, followed by Frontier in third, HPC7 in sixth, and HPC6 in eighth, the same as the most recent TOP500 list. Lux was announced a little over a year ago in a $1 billion deal between the DOE and AMD to develop two supercomputers. This is the first of the two, and the first time it’s been on the TOP500. The system was built by HPE and developed by AMD and DOE as part of the U.S. government’s Genesis Mission. The machine is housed in Oak Ridge National Laboratory’s Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility (OLCF), alongside machines like Frontier. Lux relies on over 4,000 Instinct MI355X GPUs separated into over 500 nodes. For HPC workloads using FP64, the machine is capable of 317 PetaFLOPS. For AI training, the machine peaks at 20 ExaFLOPS of FP8, and for inference, 40 ExaFLOPS of FP4. With 288 GB of HBM3E per GPU, the entire system has access to 1.1 PB. The machine uses AMD EPYC host CPUs — we weren’t able to find details on the specific generation— and AMD’s Pensando networking, with nodes built inside HPE’s ProLiant Compute XD685. TOP500 Top 10 (Nov. 2026) Rank Prev. Rank Name System 1 1 LineShine LingKun, LX2 304C 1.55GHz, LingQi, Kylin OS 2 2 El Capitan HPE Cray EX255a, AMD 4th Gen EPYC 24C 1.8GHz, AMD Instinct MI300A, Slingshot-11, TOSS 3 3 Frontier HPE Cray EX235a, AMD Optimized 3rd Generation EPYC 64C 2GHz, AMD Instinct MI250X, Slingshot-11, HPE Cray OS 4 4 Aurora HPE Cray EX - Intel Exascale Compute Blade, Xeon CPU Max 9470 52C 2.4GHz, Intel Data Center GPU Max, Slingshot-11 5 5 JUPITER Booster BullSequana XH3000, GH Superchip 72C 3GHz, NVIDIA GH200 Superchip, Quad-Rail NVIDIA InfiniBand NDR200, RedHat Enterprise Linux 6 6 HPC7 HPE Cray EX255a, AMD 4th Gen EPYC 24C 1.8GHz, AMD Instinct MI300A, Slingshot-11, RHEL 9 7 7 Eagle Microsoft NDv5, Xeon Platinum 8480C 48C 2GHz, NVIDIA H100, NVIDIA Infiniband NDR 8 8 HPC6 HPE Cray EX235a, AMD Optimized 3rd Generation EPYC 64C 2GHz, AMD Instinct MI250X, Slingshot-11, RHEL 8.9 9 9 Supercomputer Fugaku Supercomputer Fugaku, A64FX 48C 2.2GHz, Tofu interconnect D 10 10 Alps HPE Cray EX254n, NVIDIA Grace 72C 3.1GHz, NVIDIA GH200 Superchip, Slingshot-11, HPE Cray OS The machine has 3.5 million node-hours (one node running for one hour) per year, half of which are reserved for Genesis Mission research. Genesis Mission was established through an executive order in November 2025 with the stated goal of creating a “dedicated, coordinated national effort to unleash a new age of AI‑accelerated innovation and discovery that can solve the most challenging problems of this century.” More specifically, the order lays out training scientific foundation models on Federal datasets, and creating “AI agents to test new hypotheses, automate research workflows, and accelerate scientific breakthroughs.” Lux is the first dedicated supercomputer for the Genesis Mission, but it joins existing machines that have been at least partially dedicated to research, including the Intel-powered Aurora at Argonne National Laboratory, which arrived fourth in the most recent TOP500. Lux is built primarily for AI research, not as a successor to Frontier. Discovery is on track to debut as a next-gen flagship exascale supercomputer in 2028, also developed jointly by the DOE, AMD, and HPE.

articles.title: Five essential steps to protect your holiday packages from porch pirates
articles.content: Porch piracy is still a major problem. 30% of American adults have had a package stolen at some point in their lives, and 49% worry more about package theft during the holidays than at other times of year, according to Security.org’s 2026 Package Theft Report . The report estimates that 47.7 million people had a package stolen in the past year, and that the stolen packages were worth $7.7 billion. And with the average adult expecting 28 deliveries between October and December, there’s simply plenty more opportunity for boxes to sit unattended. Of course, there are things you can and should do to keep your packages safe. The best protections stop a theft before the package lands, either by arranging a verified hand-off, shortening the time a box spends outside, or sending it somewhere secure. Here are some practical ways to protect your packages from porch pirates this holiday season. Video Doorbell 2K - Wireless or Wired: If you're looking for a deal on a video doorbell this Black Friday, the crystal-clear 2K video on Arlo's option helps you keep an eye out for holiday deliveries and feel connected to your home, even when you're away. Arlo Chime 2 offers convenient in-home audio notifications, while the Arlo Secure App provides real-time, personalized notifications and the ability to see and talk with visitors on your doorstep. View Deal Stopping a delivery from going missing The strongest option for an expensive order is probably to require a verified hand-off. UPS Protected Delivery, which launches Nov. 16, requires the recipient to give the driver a PIN, or numeric code, before an eligible package is released. FedEx Authenticated Delivery uses a unique QR code instead. Both of these services are a little limited in how and where you can use them, and they may cost more too. The shipper, not the recipient, has to select either one, so ask the retailer before you order. For everything else, the carrier’s tracking app is the first line of defense. Turn on notifications from Amazon, UPS, FedEx and USPS, and act on the “out for delivery” message rather than waiting for “delivered.” Security.org identifies delivery alerts as a popular prevention method, with 39% of shoppers using delivery notifications or tracking apps. An alert alone won’t protect a box, but it at least gives you a notification you can act on relatively quickly. “The goal shouldn’t be watching your front door all day,” says Ken Sedberry, director of Xfinity Shield. “It should be knowing when a package arrives and having a plan to bring it inside.” Amazon’s scheduling tools can shorten that exposure further. Map Tracking shows the driver’s live position on eligible deliveries, while estimated two- to four-hour delivery windows give you something more useful than an all-day estimate. Prime members can also use Amazon Day to batch orders onto one day each week when someone is home. Security.org found that 43% of shoppers schedule deliveries for when someone will be there. Photo on Delivery adds a record of where the driver left the package, which is especially helpful if it ended up behind a planter or at a side entrance. It doesn’t prove the package stayed there, though. For valuable shipments, a traditional signature requirement is still worth requesting if the newer verification services aren’t available. The sender usually has to add it, and fees vary by carrier and service. Secure the drop spot The best way to secure where packages are left is to not leave them there in the first place. That may sound silly, but there are actually a few different ways you can prevent packages from being left alone on your doorstep. Amazon Locker and Counter are free alternatives, and they’re part of a network of more than 25,000 pickup locations across the country. “For those receiving a high volume of deliveries, especially during the holidays, giving carriers a secure place to leave packages is much more effective than simply hoping a camera discourages someone from taking…

articles.title: Microsoft Outage Leads To Chlorine Gas Poisoning At German Theme Park
articles.content: Slashdot readers djgl and Mirnotoriety shared a story about how a Microsoft Outlook outage contributed to a chlorine leak at Germany's Phantasialand theme park, injuring 15 guests, four of whom were hospitalized. German broadcasting institution WDR reports (translated to English): We were all affected by this problem: On Friday, there was a disruption that crippled the US software company Microsoft, including its email program Outlook. Phantasialand was also affected. Due to the disruption, no emails were received, as the company informed WDR on Saturday. As a result, no one was aware that the sauna area's maintenance safety system had already issued an email alert. This was because the automatic dosing system had pumped too much chlorine into the pool. Guests at the Hotel Ling Bao in Phantasialand, Bruhl, were injured as a result. They complained of health problems after visiting the pool. The pool was temporarily closed but has since been reopened, as the fire department informed WDR on Saturday. Due to complaints from hotel guests, emergency services and the fire department were called. Thirteen guests complained of respiratory irritation; ultimately, the number of affected individuals rose to a total of 15. Cybersecurity architect and computer scientist Stephan Skrobisch said Microsoft is not responsible for the incident. "It's clearly the system's design that's the problem. They failed to implement an additional notification mechanism." Slashdot reader davidwr agrees, writing in a comment: "Proper alarms would be a hardwired alarm that would be visible or audiable to someone who was on-site who could've gotten everyone out of the water. The blame for the injuries goes to the water park and/or whatever consultant told them it was okay not to have an on-site, hardwired alarm." Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: iPad and Mac Get Apple Intelligence in China in 27.3 Betas
articles.content: Today's iPadOS 27.3 and macOS 27.3 betas expand Apple Intelligence support in China to the iPad and the Mac. ‌Apple Intelligence‌ features debuted in China on the iPhone in the first iOS 27.3 beta, but they weren't initially available in iPadOS 27.3 or macOS 27.3. The Shanghai Cyberspace Administration said on November 9 that Apple had registered to bring ‌Apple Intelligence‌ to tablets and laptops. Developers in China can test ‌Apple Intelligence‌ after updating to the second iPadOS 27.3 and macOS 27.3 betas. ‌Apple Intelligence‌ is available on Macs and iPads with an M-series Apple silicon chip, as well as the A17 Pro and A20 Pro ‌iPad‌ minis. ‌Apple Intelligence‌ in China does not include Siri AI, the ‌Siri‌ app, or the newer ‌Apple Intelligence‌ features in iOS 27 , but it does include many of the features that debuted in the U.S. starting in iOS 18.1. ‌Siri‌, Writing Tools, and other features integrate with Alibaba's Qwen model, similar to the ChatGPT integration in other countries. Here's what's live: Live Translation for Messages, FaceTime , and the Phone app. Live Translation also works with AirPods 4 with ANC, AirPods Pro 2, and later models. Writing Tools for rewriting, proofreading, and summarizing text. With Qwen integration, users can also generate text. Visual Intelligence for identifying objects, places, and more. Clean Up in Photos for removing unwanted objects from images. Genmoji for creating custom emoji. Natural language search and memory movie creation in ‌Photos‌. Email summaries, suggested smart replies, and priority emails in the Mail app. Notification summaries, urgent notifications, and the Reduce Interruptions Focus mode. Summaries for audio recordings in the Notes app. Call transcripts in the Phone app, which are saved to the Notes app. Type to ‌Siri‌ and more natural ‌Siri‌ responses. ‌Siri‌ can relay requests to Qwen to give more in-depth answers. iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and macOS 27.3 will launch to the public in December. articles.title: IronWallet Review: A Simple, Open Wallet That Is Growing Fast
articles.content: IronWallet seems to have appeared out of nowhere, but according to Ermo Eero, the project has been around for four and a half years. The idea was to build a simple, easy-to-use crypto wallet that anyone can open, with no KYC, no ID checks, and no sign-ups. What started as a niche project has grown into a competitive product. Its most notable feature is gasless transfers, which let users move funds without holding the network's native coin to pay fees. IronWallet also offers gasless swaps, routed through SwapKit, one of the market's leading swap aggregators. Using The App IronWallet comes across as a solid all-rounder. Everything runs inside the app: sending, receiving, swapping, and buying crypto. Everything seemed to work well. Buying requires some form of KYC, which is expected, but the choice of payment providers offered in the app was wider than I anticipated. Where it Falls Short The biggest gap is network coverage. IronWallet supports 12 networks. They include many of the most popular chains, but established non-custodial wallets support considerably more, and IronWallet still has ground to make up against the market leaders. The second gap is platform. There is no desktop or web version. Nearly every competitor offers one, and for users who manage funds from a computer, that is a real limitation. IronWallet's answer to that gap is its MCP server . The MCP is open source, and it works somewhat like a desktop companion: it lets AI agents in desktop tools control the wallet, and it includes a local wallet manager that opens in your own browser for adding, importing, backing up, and deleting wallets. Experienced users of desktop AI agents will likely find it straightforward to set up. For newcomers, the advice is simple: read the FAQ first. Verdict IronWallet is a clear, open, and easy-to-use non-custodial wallet, and it is improving quickly. Its gasless transfers and gasless swaps make everyday use simpler, and buying crypto inside the app is a practical bonus. Network count and platform reach are the areas to watch, and with a project that has been building steadily for years, the momentum suggests they will keep improving. For mobile users who value simplicity and no-KYC access, IronWallet is already a strong choice, and it is well worth a look. articles.title: Hyperscale data centers use 2% of US electricity
articles.content: One flashpoint for the tech industry’s all-in push on large language models has been the sudden rush to turn investment money into hyperscale data centers. The rush hasn’t allowed anyone to plan how to supply the required electricity cleanly or with minimal impact on ratepayers. Instead, it has been difficult to even collect information on what’s being built. A new study has tallied energy use and estimated emissions for hyperscalers operating in the United States between May 2024 and April 2025. They weren’t able to differentiate between AI compute and more traditional data services, but it provides a clear point of reference to track moving forward. Finding the centers The team started with a list of 675 facilities from a commercial database based on news reports, company statements, and satellite imagery. They dropped any that didn’t have a reported electrical capacity or that they couldn’t verify was a suitably large building with the expected cooling and electrical connection equipment. That reduced the list to 403 data centers with an average electrical capacity of about 40 megawatts. Read full article Comments

articles.title: Shareholders sue Intel, its CEO, and CFO after stock drops 28.6 percent in one day
articles.content: Intel is being sued by shareholders, who are accusing the chipmaker of misleading them about the impact of the PC sales slump that contributed to a drop of 28.6 percent in the price of Intel's stock on October 30. The lawsuit ( PDF ), filed on Friday in the San Jose, California, federal court, is seeking class-action certification and lists the City of Southfield Fire and Police Retirement System and “all others similarly situated” as plaintiffs. In addition to Intel, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan and Intel’s EVP and CFO David Zinsner are listed as defendants. The plaintiffs claim that Intel made “materially false and misleading statements and omissions” between July 23 and October 29. They are seeking unspecified compensatory damages, plus legal and other associated fees, for shareholders during that period. Read full article Comments
articles.author: Scharon Harding
