articles.content: AT&T on Friday accused Comcast of false advertising in a lawsuit challenging the marketing claim that Comcast's cable broadband service and Wi-Fi is "fiber-powered." "This case challenges Comcast’s false advertising campaign for its residential Internet service, marketed under the Xfinity brand to consumers nationwide," AT&T's lawsuit said. "At the center of that campaign is Comcast’s claim that Xfinity Internet and its associated Wi-Fi service are 'Fiber-Powered.'" While Comcast has deployed plenty of fiber throughout the US, its cable Internet service makes the final connection to homes with coaxial cable. This results in upload speeds being far slower than download speeds. Read full article Comments

articles.title: Trybit Upgrades Crypto Infrastructure with New API and Interface for High-Volume Mass Payouts
articles.content: Panama, November,11 — Trybit , a global crypto payment gateway for online businesses, has released a new mass payout workflow with a new interface and API. The update adds a step-by-step form for creating mass payouts, line-by-line validation before submission, an individual status for each recipient and a searchable payout history. Trybit has also improved notifications in the personal account and added new account emails. What's new at a glance: a step-by-step form for creating mass payouts: upload the recipient list as a file, paste it as text or enter addresses manually, with a Download template button; validation errors flagged line by line before submission; an individual status for each recipient, plus a payout history with search and status filters; a summary of each mass payout sent by email; a single notification feed in the personal account that updates in real time, plus new account emails; the network detected automatically from each address; a new API with the same capabilities; an interface that works on tablets and is available in different localizations. Why Mass Payouts Break Sending one crypto transfer is simple. Sending hundreds at once is where things go wrong. One mistyped address in a long list can hold up the whole mass payout or send funds where they cannot be recovered. When part of a mass payout goes through and part does not, finance teams have to work out by hand who was paid. Re-sending without that answer risks paying the same person twice. Marketplaces, affiliate programs, gaming platforms and companies with remote contractors face this every payout cycle. Many of them still reconcile crypto payouts in spreadsheets. 1. Three ways to add recipients Mass payouts are now created through a step-by-step form with three ways to add recipients: File upload. Upload the recipient list as a .csv or .txt file of up to 5 MB. Each line holds the recipient address, the amount and, if needed, the currency. Paste as text. Paste a ready recipient list into the form as text. Manual entry. Enter addresses directly in the form. This works for one-off payouts to a few recipients. A Download template button gives teams a template that matches the format the system accepts: recipient address, amount and, if needed, currency. Teams no longer have to build the file from the format description in the documentation. The network for each recipient is detected automatically from the address, so nobody has to select it line by line. A file is more practical for regular payouts, when the list is exported from accounting software. For fully automated workflows, mass payouts via API remain available. 2. Validation before submission Every line in the recipient list is checked before the payout is submitted for processing. If a line has a problem, the error is shown next to that specific line. A team fixes the one entry that needs attention instead of rebuilding the whole file or finding the mistake after the money is gone. For cryptocurrency payouts, this is essential: a transfer to the wrong address cannot be reversed, and the check before funds are debited is the only point at which an error can be corrected without loss. 3. Individual payout statuses Once the mass payout is sent, each line in the list shows its own status. If most transfers go through and a few do not, the team sees exactly which ones need attention. Reconciliation becomes a check of one screen instead of comparing wallet history against a spreadsheet. A summary of each mass payout is also sent by email. 4. Payout history and search Sent mass payouts are saved to the history, which supports search and status filters. This makes it faster to answer a partner who asks whether a payout was sent, and to pull records together for an audit. 5. Notifications and emails The update also changes how teams learn about account events. All events now come through a single notification feed in the personal account, with new notification types for partial invoice payments,…

articles.title: The Flaw Chipmakers Spent 50 Years Fighting Is Now Their Best Feature: Memory Chip Fingerprinting
articles.content: Memory chips of the same model, with identical serial numbers and the same price, come off the manufacturing line. But when they are powered on, each begins its unique pattern of making tiny mistakes. For years, these mistakes were a target for the engineers trying to eliminate them. However, security specialists found ways to use them for anti-counterfeit protection, securing encryption keys, and even tracing people. Why there are different kinds of memory The ideal memory chip should be fast, cheap, spacious, and non-volatile. None exist. Hence, computers use different types of memory chips, each of them having some advantages in particular tasks. SRAM uses the miniature closed circuit of transistors containing two possible states for every bit - like a light switch. It is the fastest memory but requires six transistors to store one bit and, therefore, is expensive and big. SRAM is used in the cache memory and microcontrollers' memory. DRAM stores each bit in the form of the amount of charge in the capacitor. Only one transistor and a capacitor are necessary to store one bit. Therefore, it is cheap and small enough to become the primary memory of the computer. Unfortunately, the charge stored in it leaks away with time, and the memory needs refreshing every 64 milliseconds. Flash uses a special transistor in which the charge is trapped in the insulator. Once in there, electrons remain trapped for years, making flash a good choice for phone memory, SSDs, and USB drives. The writing and erasing process of the flash is slower than that of other memories, as erasure happens in blocks. Additionally, the erasure process damages the insulator, hence limiting the usage of the memory in several thousands of erasing cycles. Flaws of each memory kind Modern chip factories work with technologies on an atomic level, and atoms rarely fall in place identically each time. Therefore, one transistor may be slightly stronger than its neighbour, one capacitor - leakier, some insulator layers - thinner. The manufacturers try to hide those defects under the safe margins and make all memory chips behave alike. However, if pushed to the very limit of these margins, individual flaws will start causing flipped bits. For instance, when an SRAM chip is powered on, it does not know what its starting state is. Powering on a cell means letting it choose the desirable state, and it always depends on which of the two sides wins, the winning side being a bit stronger. For DRAM, if it is disturbed somehow, it will forget its contents. Without refreshing the memory, the leakiest cells will forget their contents first. Moreover, in DRAM, there is a more serious flaw: the reading of some rows of the memory will affect the adjacent rows, flipping the bits in the memory that was not accessed by the program. This is the infamous Rowhammer effect. In 2014, researchers detected it in 110 out of 129 memory modules they tested. As with DRAM, in flash memory, changing the content of one cell can affect the state of the neighbouring cells. Besides, the cells of flash memory wear out differently: some of them can be programmed after only a few writing cycles, whilst some will require many more of them. Turning flaws into fingerprints Now that we know the flaws of each memory type, we can force errors and pinpoint their location. This pattern of errors is different in each chip but unique to one particular chip, just like a fingerprint. Researchers call it a physical unclonable function since even the manufacturer will not be able to create another chip with the same fingerprint pattern. Turn on an SRAM chip and read its content right after. Most of the cells wake up identically each time, creating the long series of ones and zeros that are unique to this one chip. Comparison of two power-ups of the same chip shows that differences occur in fewer than ten per cent of the bits. On the contrary, comparing two different chips shows differences in about half of the bits. This…

articles.title: How the World’s Most Advanced AI Infrastructure Supply Chain Invents the Future
articles.content: Deb Shoquist leads operations at NVIDIA, overseeing the supply chain and manufacturing behind its AI platforms. That description sums up the job, but it doesn’t begin to encompass what Shoquist has made possible over decades. Shoquist, her team and their global network of manufacturing partners enable NVIDIA to introduce world-leading technologies year-round. Much of the team’s success comes down to her deep relationships with some of the world’s most accomplished manufacturers, including TSMC, Foxconn, Wistron, SPIL, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Unimicron, Lumentum, Coherent and Amkor. TSMC has partnered with NVIDIA since 1998. SPIL and KYEC were assembling and testing its chips more than two decades ago. For Shoquist, those relationships grow stronger through each challenge solved together on the factory floor, as every generation of technology demands more from the people and tools behind it. Ask her about the global network she relies on, and she starts with the people. There’s the supplier in Taiwan so eager to get production moving that he calls her at 3 a.m. with a fix to the latest problem. There are the factory workers in Vietnam whose only ask of her are more tools to get more work done. She remembers the partners that supported NVIDIA when it was small, and the work they’ve done to help each other grow. Shoquist meets with key suppliers quarterly and spends six weeks each year on the road visiting partners in Taiwan, China, Korea, Vietnam and the U.S., where conversations move from meeting rooms to factory floors. Recently, she paused her travels to accept the 2026 Dr. Lisa Su Woman of Innovation Award — and to share how she finds the right people and companies to imagine and produce at massive scale technology that has never been built before. Foxconn Q: How would you describe your job to someone outside NVIDIA? A: At the most basic level, our job is to convert designs into the physical world. Our design team creates a blueprint, and our job is to transition it into a reliable, high-performance supply chain. A matchmaker is probably the best analogy. You have to find the partner that matches your ramp style and has the technology that can meet the needs of very precise designs. The supplier has to be financially strong enough to invest in our ramps. They have to be highly technical. And they have to be willing to do something that has never been done before. If you don’t have all three, you can’t create products at the volume and speed that we need. You need those three legs, and in some cases, if you only have two, you have to invest in the company to make them a partner. Q: What’s an example of that in practice ? A: Amphenol’s cable cartridge is the most complex interconnect assembly they have ever built. When I recently visited the Vietnam factory, now in full production, I was struck by the level of precision required to build a product of this complexity. In this large cable cartridge, there are 1,500 small cable legs. Each one requires a very precise assembly to yield a quality level of less than 1 DPPM, or defect part per million. Amphenol built over a hundred automated lines to produce this product at the speed and scale we require. That takes know-how and technology, but it also takes heart, willingness and dedication. Creating anything of that complexity and precision with a supplier forges the partnership. The partners NVIDIA maintains are the ones who supported us when we were small, and yet are willing to scale with us today. Q: What changed as NVIDIA went from selling chips to building systems and platforms? A: When we were primarily a chip manufacturer, we were small, and the semiconductor industry was at scale. In that environment, it was about picking the best technology match for the products we envisioned. As we became a data center systems company, we needed more partners. But we’ve also now entered into new technology areas where the scale of the supply base is still developing. For example,…

articles.title: Apple Eyes 2027 Launch For AI-Powered Smart Glasses
articles.content: Apple is reportedly targeting WWDC 2027 to unveil its first smart glasses, with shipments planned before the end of that year. According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman (paywalled), the company has hopes of making them its flagship new product for 2027. Forbes reports: It's no secret that Meta with its Ray-Ban Meta and Oakley Meta glasses, for instance, lead the field when it comes to smart specs. "Apple is counting on integration with the apps people already use on their iPhones to be a key differentiator for the glasses," Gurman said. The App Store has millions of apps while Meta's apps are far fewer. It seems the smart glasses will use a version of the software used on the Vision Pro. "The thinking inside Apple is that while Meta has the increasingly popular Muse agent, Apple has the App Store. Because the Siri integrations are being developed for the iPhone first, software makers won't need to build separate applications for the glasses," Gurman insisted. It seems the glasses will do a lot, from making restaurant reservations to booking cars, ordering coffee or buying movie tickets. "It's also Apple's big AI monetization opportunity," Gurman believes. Part of the experience will depend on Apple's own AI agent system, it seems. There won't be augmented reality in the glasses and they will be lighter than the competition, but with longer battery life and more sensors. Gurman refers to cameras, in the plural, while current models only have one camera, or none at all in the case of Even Realities which tout their privacy aspects. "Apple is also emphasizing the sound quality," Gurman says, "which employees have said is industry-leading, with support for phone calls, music playback and FaceTime audio communication." Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Supreme Court keeps injunction against DEI grant defunding in place
articles.content: On Monday, the Supreme Court announced it would not hear an appeal of a lower court decision that blocked the government from canceling the grants of a handful of researchers whose funding had been revoked during the Trump administration's purge of DEI-related work. While the decision applies to only seven researchers in California, the lower court had ruled that the government's actions violated the First Amendment and so may have broad implications. The Supreme Court provided no discussion of its rejection, and no justices filed a dissent regarding the decision. The suit was initially filed by a large group of researchers at the University of California, Berkeley and UC San Francisco, contesting grants originally issued by many federal agencies, from the National Institutes of Health to the Department of Transportation. At issue were grants that had been terminated because the agencies decided they violated a Trump executive order blocking the use of DEI. This occurred despite the fact that the government hadn't bothered to define DEI , and targeted grants were often identified by little more than a keyword search . Read full article Comments

articles.title: Attackers are using AI agents to automate cybercrime at 'industrial scale,' FBI and AWS warn
articles.content: Attackers are using open source AI penetration testing framework ARTEX to automate their attacks on banks, governments, energy and healthcare providers, and other critical sectors around the globe, according to security alerts from the FBI and Amazon Threat Intelligence. Between October 3 and November 5, Amazon’s MadPot honeypot threat sensors detected two ARTEX campaigns: one that allowed thieves to steal AI credentials at “industrial scale” to gain free access to models, and a second that generated deepfake videos to trick live selfie checks. In the first one, miscreants used AI agents to steal API keys, and then feed these keys into the ARTEX framework’s model gateway to power more agents searching for more AI model access keys. “Agents validated identities through each provider’s token and identity services, enumerated storage, assessed permission scope, and went after managed AI model services, secrets and parameter stores, and application identities,” AWS Chief Information Security Officer CJ Moses wrote in a blog post on Friday. Targets included LLM gateways and proxy platforms such as One API, New API, Veloera, Sub2API, and LiteLLM, and AI application builders Dify, FastGPT, Langflow, RAGFlow, Open WebUI, LobeChat, and Ollama. This campaign also used cloud credentials to gain stolen access to the models. In a second campaign, attackers used ARTEX to create real-time deepfake videos to trick identity verification (KYC) checks at two cryptocurrency exchanges, and forged ID photos to pass document checks. “The agents reverse-engineered one vendor’s liveness protocol in detail, documenting the face-detection event stream it sends, how it tracks face position during the check, and the coordinate system it uses to tell the user where to move,” Moses wrote. The agents did manage to complete the full movement sequence with the face positioned within 7 pixels of the target, but this feat was not enough, as the vendor’s server-side verdict rejected the deepfake in every attempt. In a separate session, agents built a real-time deepfake video pipeline on a single consumer-grade GPU using an open-source face animation model. This video achieved 11.5 frames per second, which Moses said is “close to what a live video check expects.” Meanwhile, agents also worked on the ID document checks, building synthetic camera metadata whose image dimensions matched the real values inside the JPEG file, and preserving the original camera compression tables that are usually replaced by re-saving an edited image. While the end goal was stealing cryptocurrency, the campaign illustrates how ARTEX runs several sessions simultaneously, with multiple agents working toward the same result. “One searched for ways to cash out, one worked on clearing account balances, one set up the deepfake video pipeline, and one carried out the verification bypass,” Moses wrote. None of the attack techniques are new, but both of these campaigns show how AI agents can boost the speed and persistence of the attacker. “The agents succeeded where basic security hygiene was missing, including default or hardcoded credentials, keys left in code and public artifacts, unauthenticated interfaces and inference endpoints, and unpatched software,” Moses added. “Getting those fundamentals right remains the most effective defense.” The FBI weighs in The FBI also hammered this message in a separate Friday alert noting “ARTEX significantly reduces the time required to chain attack techniques, with some intrusions progressing from initial targeting to privileged access in under three hours.” The federal cops cited the August attacks against South Korean financial institutions that stole personal data belonging to about 67,000 people. The FBI also highlighted a September ARTEX campaign that targetedd ConnectWise Cloud Backup customers in a supply chain attack that ultimately compromised more than 2,250 downstream Microsoft tenants . articles.title: When will humans actually fly on Starship?
articles.content: The stunning return of Starship from the skies to a launch tower in South Texas answered some questions about the future of SpaceX's ambitious rocket program. Namely, it is now rapidly moving toward rapidly reusable launch. However, it raises other questions. For example, as Starship becomes fully reusable, when might humans fly on the vehicle? The short answer is pretty simple: If SpaceX prioritizes human spaceflight on Starship, it could happen reasonably quickly. The longer answer becomes more complicated and depends on what one means by human spaceflight. The first people to fly on Starship probably won't launch from Earth, or land here. Rather, they will probably be NASA's lunar astronauts. So there are different timelines for humans flying aboard Starship and landing on Earth. Read full article Comments

articles.title: New in iOS 27.3 beta 2: Front camera unlock, Siri AI in Safari, more
articles.content: Apple's iOS 27.3 is now on its second developer beta, adding new locking and unlocking options for iPhone Duo, new Siri features for Safari, and an update to Apple Podcasts. iOS 27.3 beta 2 brings new iPhone Duo features, Siri AI capabilities in Safari, and more. On Monday, a week after the release of IOS 27.2.1, Apple made iOS 27.3 developer beta 2 available for download. The first developer beta of iOS 27.3 introduced vertical Safari tabs, Siri Recaps, Live Rewind, and a redesigned Health app, among other things. iOS 27.3 beta 2 also brings new features and enhancements, some exclusive to Apple's recently released foldable, the iPhone Duo . articles.title: Apple News+ Puzzles Come to UK, Australia, and French Canada
articles.content: In iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and the other 27.3 updates, puzzles are expanding to Australian, UK, and French-Canadian Apple News + subscribers. ‌Apple News‌+ subscribers in Australia get access to a daily quick crossword, crossword mini, Sudoku, Quartiles, and Emoji Game. UK subscribers get the daily quick crossword, crossword mini, and Sudoku, while French-Canadian subscribers can play Quartiles and Emoji Game. Quartiles and Emoji Game are original Apple puzzles. Quartiles requires players to form words by combining letter tiles, and Emoji Game lets subscribers complete phrases using a selection of emoji. Prior to now, ‌Apple News‌+ puzzles have been limited to the U.S. and English-language subscribers in Canada. The games can be accessed in the Puzzles section under the Following tab in the ‌Apple News‌ app in iOS 27.3 beta 2. The update will launch to the public in December. articles.title: Meet the new James Bond: Robert Pattinson
articles.content: The Internet has been abuzz for months about which actor would replace Daniel Craig as British agent 007 James Bond in the franchise. We finally have the answer: Robert Pattinson , who built on his 2005 role as the doomed Cedric Diggory in Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire into an illustrious career mixing roles in franchises and Hollywood blockbusters with daring arthouse fare. “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” Pattinson said in a statement . “To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.” The choice will reunite Pattinson with Denis Villeneuve, who recently worked with him on the forthcoming Dune: Part III and will direct the next (as yet untitled) Bond installment. “I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey," Villeneuve said in a statement . We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007. I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin.” Read full article Comments
articles.author: Jennifer Ouellette

articles.title: HTML-in-Canvas ships and could make the web a lot more creative...and a lot stupider
articles.content: After two years of experimentation, the Chrome team shipped the HTML-in-Canvas API with Chrome 157. With it comes a new vision of how Web pages could be designed, for better or worse, allowing richer, more interactive elements but also more opportunities for annoying ads. “Previously, when creating visually demanding web apps, you had to choose between standard HTML elements and raw canvas contexts,” enthused one Google DevRel in a tutorial . “HTML-in-Canvas eliminates these trade-offs.” The Web API has been submitted for inclusion in the WHATWG HTML Living Standard , the ever-updating standard formerly known as HTML5 – for all the technologies that officially make up HTML (including Canvas itself). A Web API for the browser’s rendering engine Originally developed by Apple and standardized in 2014, the canvas tag is an HTML element that offers a space to render fluid graphics via JavaScript drawing commands. It creates a dedicated grid on screen, within which JavaScript can use a set of Canvas methods to draw lines, curves, text, gradients, and images. Or, the user’s GPU, via WebGL or WebGPU, can use the canvas to render 3D images and other custom effects. The downside of Canvas is that the regular HTML controls didn’t work inside the canvas itself. Formatting any text had to be done by hand. Interactivity was out, as were accessibility aids. Primarily developed by the Google Chromium team, HTML-in-Canvas allows JavaScript to place HTML commands within the canvas element, thanks to an attribute option within Canvas. If the canvas tag includes a content attribute of "drawable," the browser’s rendering engine prepares the HTML content inside the box so JavaScript can render it. While fully supported by Chrome and Chrome Android beginning with release 157, none of the other major browsers support the API yet (Microsoft Edge 157 – which is made of Chromium – unofficially appears to support at least some HTML-in-Canvas actions as well). The Web’s about to get lit Google posted a few possibilities of what can be done with HTML-in-Canvas. Developers can wrap HTML controls onto a 3D object. In one example , the user can turn the pages of a virtual book and even copy text out of the book itself. A video, complete with a set of controls , can be wrapped into an odd-sized canvas. The spec seems to work particularly well with JavaScript plug-ins, allowing coders to create entire 3D environments with Three.js , or to create charts with D3.js . Enthusiasts are already hacking against the spec with mad abandon. Developer Wes Bos put a notes app in the canvas , then used it as target practice by overlaying the app with some Duck Hunt-styled game code. HTML-in-Canvas “opens up the door to a lot of stupid use cases … but also a lot of really creative, interesting things where you can apply stylistic effects to HTML,” Bos explained on X . A trippy demo from html-in-canvas.dev shows a dragon slithering through the opening chapter of an online book, with the text smoothly reflowing in its wake. Try to shoo the beast off with your cursor and it will burn the virtual text with its fiery breath. The source code reveals that “Margin Dragon” was rendered in 881 lines of vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript code. Another demo on the sample site is a “mouse-driven elastic displacement effect,” in which a “radial bulge” and drop shadow follow the cursor across the canvas. Of course, such stylistic enchantments will not always be used for whimsy. Inevitably, unscrupulous marketers will discover powerful new ways to annoy us about all the virtues of late-stage capitalism. “The world is not ready for HTML-in-Canvas,” a punter wrote on X . Here be dragons As per norm, HTML-in-Canvas has plenty of bugs (and it hasn’t even gone cross-platform yet). In some cases, the CSS doesn’t get painted on where it should , and timing with the reactive frameworks could be better synchronized . And there is a lot for the lowly web maintainer to learn. The core developers…
articles.author: Joab Jackson

articles.title: Leaked Credentials Are an Enterprise Problem: GitGuardian Extends Its Good Samaritan Program
articles.content: New York, USA, November 16th, 2026/CyberNewswire/--AI attribution has linked more than 3,913 high-impact leaks to 1,532 companies since spring; security experts handle critical disclosures to enterprise security teams. GitGuardian , the secrets security platform, today announced the Enterprise Good Samaritan Program , an expansion of its longstanding responsible disclosure efforts aimed at strengthening security across the broader digital ecosystem. Combining AI-powered attribution with expert security analysis, the program identifies high-impact credential leaks that could give attackers a path into an organization's systems or data. It traces these exposures to affected companies and delivers actionable disclosures to their security teams, showing how an attacker could exploit the credentials and what they could gain access to. For the first time, GitGuardian can extend these warnings to any company in the world, regardless of its size or whether it's a GitGuardian customer. Since 2018, GitGuardian's original Good Samaritan Program has detected more than 83 million exposed secrets on public GitHub, sending 11.9 million alerts to 5.9 million developers. But notifying a developer doesn't necessarily lead to revocation. Approximately 90% of valid secrets remain unrevoked a week after the developer responsible for the leak has been alerted. To date, the Enterprise Good Samaritan Program has linked more than 3,913 high-impact leaks to 1,532 companies. GitGuardian followed up with them, typically reaching at least five people at each organization. The scale of the problem is growing. GitGuardian's 2026 State of Secrets Sprawl report found that 28.65 million new secrets were exposed on public GitHub in 2025, a 34% year-over-year increase. The Enterprise Good Samaritan Program gets exposed credentials to the security teams that can revoke them. "For years, we've warned developers, but they're not always the ones who can revoke it. Our expertise combined with AI now helps us identify at scale the organizations behind serious exposures at scale, and our researchers work to reach the people who can respond. Attackers now have the ability, with AI offensive harnesses like ARTEX, to use these credentials to target companies at scale. Those companies deserve to know, whether they're our customers or not. And if a company has no clear way to receive a warning, the warning doesn’t help. Every company needs a door for these reports, and someone behind it.” — Eric Fourrier, CEO at GitGuardian Extending Responsible Disclosure To The Enterprise The Enterprise Good Samaritan Program combines continuous public monitoring, AI-assisted analysis, and human-led disclosure to identify serious credential exposures and help organizations respond. GitGuardian monitors public sources, including GitHub and Docker Hub, for exposed credentials. Its AI agents now screen more than 1 million public incidents each month and investigate over 100,000 in depth , helping identify the affected organizations and assess the potential impact of exposure, including credential validity, permissions, and the systems or data at risk. Human experts review high-impact findings before disclosure, providing the affected organization with the context needed to investigate and remediate the exposure. Rather than relying exclusively on notifications to individual developers, GitGuardian contacts multiple people within affected organizations, works to reach the relevant security teams, and escalates manually when automated outreach goes unanswered. The value of this escalation was demonstrated in May 2026, when GitGuardian researchers identified a public GitHub repository containing sensitive CISA-related data and valid cloud credentials. Nine automated alerts had failed to resolve the exposure. After GitGuardian researchers escalated through CERT/CC and established contacts, the repository was taken offline within 26 hours of human escalation. The need for timely disclosure is…

articles.title: Nvidia announces Rubin HPC GPU with 'record number of CUDA cores' at Supercomputing 2026
articles.content: The Supercomputing 2026 conference is under way, and despite continuing turmoil elsewhere in the company, Nvidia has lots to reveal at the show. Foremost among its announcements today, Nvidia took the wraps off a new member of the Rubin GPU family called Rubin HPC , a chip that the company says is meant to accelerate agentic workflows and simulation for scientists, engineers, and analysts working with large data sets. To accelerate those most demanding workloads, Nvidia says Rubin HPC has the highest number of CUDA cores on any of its GPUs - "more than 50,000" - which might imply that this chip uses a configuration similar to the four-die Rubin Ultra GPU, which links those dies together using NVLink-C2C. Today's Rubin GPU has 224 SMs and 28,672 CUDA cores, so scaling compute resources to the degree Rubin HPC does would necessarily require more dies on a package. Nvidia didn't reveal more details of the chip's physical layout alongside the announcement. (The representative image shared by the company wouldn't appear to take this into account.) To keep data moving between Rubin HPC GPUs, Nvidia will use its NVLink 7 interconnect. The company didn't share any new details of the bandwidth or physical layer of this interconnect within the rack, but past disclosures about the tech have indicated that it retains the 3.6 TB/s of per-GPU bandwidth that NVLink 6 delivers while enlarging the size of its scale-up domain. Nvidia didn't share any details of the Rubin HPC GPU's HBM capacity or bandwidth, and it also didn't share whether this part includes a rebalancing of compute resources towards native FP64, as AMD and Intel are touting at the conference with their own GPUs this week. Nvidia instead touts the suitability of this chip for scientists and engineers using agentic workflows, for which the company expects faster simulation performance and therefore faster opportunities for discovery in those fields thanks to better agent performance in those domains. In fields like climate research, genomic analysis, and financial simulation, Nvidia says the Rubin HPC GPU's "balanced design," with both higher compute resources and (presumably) faster data movement between nodes, will help feed the chip with the massive data sets typical of those workloads, minimizing idle compute resources and achieving better utilization. Researchers, engineers, and analysts marshaling agent swarms to explore the problem spaces in their domains will also be able to take advantage of Nvidia's CUDA-X domain-specific libraries to boost performance on Rubin HPC, tightening the reasoning loop from hypothesis to simulation to refinement and hastening the pursuit of the most promising results. Nvidia says Rubin HPC will arrive sometime in 2028.

articles.title: China’s grip on Top500 remains uncontested as US chases AI-HPC fusion
articles.content: A new Top500 list of supercomputers has dropped, but little has changed. China remains uncontested with the most powerful supercomputer on the biannual ranking, and the US is not even close behind. The Middle Kingdom's LineShine super tops the list, boasting 2.2 exaFLOPS as measured by the High Performance Linpack (HPL) benchmark. That's roughly 22 percent ahead of Uncle Sam’s biggest iron, Laurence Livermore National Laboratory’s El Capitan . But LineShine may not be the most efficient. Using 42.2 megawatts, LineShine’s lead comes at the expense of a noticeably higher power bill; not that that makes much of a difference. Number one is number one, and to add insult to injury, the National Supercomputing Centre in Shenzhen (NSCS) did it in spite of US export controls denying them access to American GPUs. The entire super is powered by 45,360 LingKun LX2 CPUs , each with 304 Arm v9.2 cores clocking to 1.5 GHz. The US is unlikely to reclaim the number one spot any time soon, though not for lack of trying. Under the Genesis Mission announced late last year, the Department of Energy is on track to deploy at least nine new supers. It just so happens that most of these will be smaller or AI-focused machines, with few truly large systems. Oak Ridge National Laboratory’s (ORNL) Lux supercomputer , built in collaboration with HPE and AMD, is one such example. Delivering 220 petaFLOPS of double-precision grunt in HPL, it’s certainly a potent system. Just two years ago it would have been a top 10 supercomputer, but it''l have to settle for number 14 on this fall’s Top500 ranking. Now, if you’re willing to turn the resolution slider down to FP4, peak performance jumps to somewhere north of 20 exaFLOPS. That’s fine for AI inference and even some training, but for running multi-physics sims on America's nuclear deterrent, the DoE has traditionally gone for something a bit bigger. ORNL’s upcoming Discovery system will certainly have enough grunt to give LineShine the boot. Details on the HPE Cray based system remain thin, but we do know it’ll be powered by a combination of AMD Venice CPUs and Instinct MI430X GPUs. Unlike most of the GPUs sold today, the MI430X hasn’t forsaken double-precision grunt for low-precision AI throughput. Each of these multi-die chips is estimated to deliver north of 200 teraFLOPS of FP64 matrix math. According to the DoE, Discovery will deliver somewhere between 3x to 5x the performance of Frontier, which would put its Rpeak somewhere between 5.1 and 8.5 exaFLOPS at FP64. As impressive as that might sound, China has proven that once you take power out of the equation, all it takes to claim the number one spot is scale. And if there is one thing LineShine does well, it’s scale. In GPU-accelerated systems like El Cap, you’re lucky to push HPL to within 70 percent of the system’s theoretical roofline. But LineShine isn’t GPU-accelerated. Sure, with 16 HBM stacks, the LX2 looks a lot like a GPU, but it's really just an enormous CPU with enough vector and matrix units to put more than a few modern GPUs to shame. With enough of them – by which we mean 22,680 dual-socket nodes – NSCS catapulted China to the top of the Top500 for the first time in nearly a decade. Not the benchmark it used to be The US has no shortage of systems capable of eclipsing El Capitan or even LineShine’s performance if someone were motivated enough to get HPL running on them. SpaceXAI’s 300 megawatt Colossus supercomputer in Memphis, Tennessee, boasts 200,000 Hopper GPUs each good for 34-67 (vector/matrix) teraFLOPS of FP64 grunt. Even assuming an abysmal 25% efficiency, the cluster should be more than capable of breaking three exaFLOPs in HPL. It might need 10x the power of El Capitan, but the thing is, beyond winning points with the White House — a ship that has almost certainly sailed for Elon Musk after the DOGE fiasco — renting out the cluster to Anthropic to train and run Claude is a far more lucrative endeavor. articles.title: Corporations Are Using Trump's Tariff Refunds On Bonuses Rather Than Reimbursing
articles.content: An anonymous reader quotes a report from ProPublica: When Stanley Black & Decker, one of the world's largest tool companies, got hit with President Donald Trump's tariffs last year, the firm made clear that it would be sharing the pain with its customers. The Connecticut-based company raised prices again and again, moves its executives said were necessary because of the new fees on imports. Now, after the Supreme Court struck down Trump's most sweeping tariffs earlier this year, the company is getting at least $298 million refunded. Instead of sharing that bounty with its customers, however, the firm has chosen different recipients: Its own leaders. The company is one of at least nine that have disclosed that they are using their refunds not to pay back the cash-strapped consumers who generally covered much of the tariff costs through higher prices, but to give bonuses, according to a ProPublica analysis of thousands of securities filings and earnings calls for publicly traded companies. Other recognizable companies include the owners of discount department stores TJ Maxx and Marshalls and the golf equipment brand Titleist. Dozens of other firms have said little about how they plan to use the money other than to characterize the windfall as the kind of earnings they use to determine executive bonuses. The Trump administration has not publicly detailed which companies are getting the roughly $170 billion in refunds or how much they've asked for, and it has denied ProPublica's requests for this information. But reporters found some of these details while reviewing the disclosures of thousands of publicly traded companies. Some have described vague plans to pay the money forward by, for example, "returning tariff refunds to our members through pricing," though they generally don't say whether that involves price cuts or limiting future increases. Others are paying back businesses they sold products to because they had itemized receipts that detailed the tariff markups. But consumers hoping for refunds appear to be largely out of luck. With the help of artificial intelligence, ProPublica identified companies that said they planned to refund customers with their tariff windfalls. Almost all of them deal with other businesses, not consumers. "Executive bonuses are probably the least just way to use this money because it wasn't anything the executives did that they should be rewarded for. It was a government mistake that resulted in a refund," said Gregory Germain, a corporate law professor at Syracuse University. "It really explains why it's so important for the government, when they're doing something like this, to think it through to make sure consumers don't pay extra money and not get it back." Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Map It Before You Automate It: 10 Best Practices for Business Process Automation
articles.content: Business processes will include several different tasks, departments and systems. This can become time consuming and cumbersome to manage manually and can cause delays, double work, miscommunication and human error. Understand your current processes, identify where improvements can be made and implement automation in a structured way. By mapping out each step of the process, your business can be more organized, dependable and efficient. Whether you’re looking to automate customer queries, payments, employee records or general internal processes, having a plan in place can help reduce manual work and improve consistency. What is Business Process Automation Mapping? Business process automation mapping is when you produce a visual representation of your business processes so you can identify which parts can be automated. This combines 2 important concepts: Business Process Mapping : This identifies and maps out all the tasks, decisions, roles and information that are part of your business’ processes. Business Process Automation: Performing repeated tasks using technology. When combined, this gives your organization a greater understanding of their processes and where automation can be most beneficial. Why Should You Map Your Operational Processes? Before beginning to automate your processes, it is important to understand your current operations. If you try to automate an inefficient process without taking a look at the structure, you could just speed up your problems. Improved Efficiency: By mapping your processes, you can identify any repeated tasks, unnecessary tasks and bottlenecks. You can then simplify these. Reduced Human Error: Automating repeated tasks can help reduce errors when inputting data, calculating and moving information. Having standardized processes also improves consistency. Improved Accountability: By using process maps you can identify who should be responsible for each task. This makes it clearer for employees and departments what their role is. Improved Productivity: Automating processes means less manual work for your employees. This allows them to spend more time on decision making, problem solving and other tasks requiring human input. Increased Visibility: Having documented processes will help you keep track of your processes and identify any delays. You’ll also have a better understanding of how each department contributes to the process. Best Practice for Business Process Automation Mapping Creating a dependable automation strategy requires more than just choosing the right software and linking your systems together. First you need to understand what your business needs from its processes. To help improve your processes and make them more efficient, there are some best practice tips to consider: 1. Identify Areas For Improvement The first thing to do is understand what areas within your business processes are taking too long or requiring too much manual work. Look at your processes and identify: Repeated admin tasks Frequent data entry errors Delays to approvals and communication Unnecessary repetition Too much manual monitoring required. Speak to your employees who regularly carry out these tasks. They can give you real insight into any issues. By knowing what the issue actually is, you won’t waste time automating processes which don’t need much changes. 2. Be Clear With Objectives Each process map should be created with a clear objective. This means understanding what you want to achieve. You may want to reduce the time taken to process invoices, improve customer onboarding or make it easier to approve employee leave. By identifying clear start and end points, you will avoid any unnecessary tasks. Being clear with your scope will also help you know which departments, employees, systems and resources are involved. 3. articles.title: The open-source movement wants Jensen Huang back
articles.content: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here . On Friday, a petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia began circulating on social media, and by Monday it listed some notable signatories, including Elon Musk and several influential Nvidia researchers. But comb through the more than 115,000 names and you’ll notice a significant faction of Huang’s supporters—higher-ups from Hugging Face, a hub for sharing AI models, and venture capital firms Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia Capital—come from a particular slice of the tech world. These names have a vested interest in the development of open-source AI, models that, unlike ChatGPT or Claude, can be downloaded and run independent of large tech companies. Supporters of such models say that concentrating AI in the hands of a few powerful companies will leave everyone else worse off (a concern that wouldn’t sound out of place among the AI industry’s critics on the left, if so many open-source advocates weren’t also venture capitalists who stand to profit when startups can build on cheaper AI without paying Big Tech). Huang had become a sort of ringleader for those who defend open source to policymakers against concerns that such models come with no guardrails and cede AI leadership to China, where the most powerful and popular open-source models are created. They now want their most influential voice returned to his post. But it’s not just Huang’s extramarital affairs that threaten his (and Nvidia’s) credibility as an advocate for open-source AI. New research into China’s startups using Nvidia’s chips, and a new rule from the US Department of Commerce announced Monday, could deal a blow to both the movement’s reputation and its technical progress. On Thursday, the day Huang resigned, ex-OpenAI researcher Will DePue published findings online suggesting that China’s AI companies had far more access to Nvidia’s advanced Blackwell chips than previously estimated. China is banned from accessing Nvidia’s most cutting-edge chips to help protect America’s AI lead. It’s unclear how they would have gained access to the chips. DePue claims the results were verified by senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic, but an independent analysis has not confirmed the results. (DePue did not respond to a request for an interview. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.) The findings do not establish that Nvidia helped Chinese companies obtain the chips, and the broader problem of chip smuggling was already known to extend well beyond Nvidia’s control. But in suggesting that Nvidia may have profited from the rise of Chinese AI startups, whose models are increasingly being used by American companies instead of domestic alternatives, the findings do leave Huang in an awkward position. He has championed open-source AI as a way to strengthen American technological leadership. “Without open source, startups can’t thrive, university researchers can’t do research, you can’t teach AI, scientists can’t use AI,” he said last December during a talk about helping the US win the AI race against China. It also makes the idea of reinstating Huang even more of a long shot. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent even said last week that Nvidia should not consider someone from inside the company to replace him. The new findings lower Huang’s chances further. What happens next? Nvidia announced in September it would acquire Hugging Face for nearly $13 billion. Its support for open source also serves a straightforward financial interest: The more businesses that build their own models instead of forking over money to Anthropic and OpenAI, the more chips Nvidia can sell. But a new rule from the US Department of Commerce could mean the models popular on Hugging Face will soon stop getting smarter. The rule aims to prevent Chinese companies from training models on Nvidia chips that they can’t own…

articles.title: Former UW AI researchers Yejin Choi and Carlos Guestrin raise $110M for AI startup Noeri
articles.content: Noeri co-CEOs Yejin Choi and Carlos Guestrin. (Noeri Photos) Yejin Choi and Carlos Guestrin , two prominent AI researchers who spent years at the University of Washington before moving to Stanford, have raised $110 million for Noeri , a startup building AI systems that keep improving on a company’s own work. Menlo Ventures led the round, with participation from Seattle-based Madrona, Kindred Ventures, Wing Venture Capital and NEA. Cisco Investments, Nvidia and Snowflake also invested. Bloomberg first reported the funding Monday; the valuation wasn’t disclosed. Noeri’s software studies a company’s data and workflows, then proposes changes to the system around a specific task: the instructions, the tools, which model handles each step and, in some cases, the models themselves. Each change is explained and sent to a person for approval, much like a code review, the company said. It works with closed and open-weight models. Customers keep ownership of the workflows and models they develop, subject to third-party model licenses, the company said. The pitch is aimed at companies stuck choosing between paying for the most capable model and accepting weaker results from a cheaper one. The idea grew partly out of an effort to help a Stanford microbiology and immunology team use OpenAI’s models more cheaply, Bloomberg reported. The small model they built learned to use older OpenAI models and, to the founders’ surprise, outperformed GPT-5 on that team’s research needs, Choi told Bloomberg. The name Noeri means “intelligence, in the plural,” reflecting the founders’ argument against a future dominated by one powerful model. Guestrin said at Madrona’s IA40 Summit in late September that intelligence shouldn’t be controlled by one or two companies that own the models. “Few companies would build their core operations on a single consultant who also advises every competitor, can change its terms at will, and can never be brought in-house,” Choi and Guestrin wrote in an essay posted with the launch. “A single, centralized AI offers exactly that arrangement.” Noeri isn’t alone in helping businesses tailor models. In a July report on Noeri’s fundraising, The Information cited Thinking Machines Lab’s Tinker, fine-tuning software that developers use through an API, and Applied Compute, which embeds engineers with its customers. Guestrin helped develop XGBoost, a widely used machine learning tool, and co-founded Turi, the Seattle startup formerly known as GraphLab and Dato, which Apple acquired in 2016 . He went on to lead Apple’s central machine learning and AI organization. Choi, a 2022 MacArthur Fellow, led common-sense reasoning research at the Allen Institute for AI (Ai2) before she left UW and Ai2 in 2024 to join Nvidia as a distinguished scientist, a role she held until starting Noeri in May. She joined Stanford’s faculty in early 2025. The two are co-CEOs. Noeri is based in Palo Alto with an office in Zurich. Madrona and NEA have backed Guestrin before: the two firms led a $6.75 million round in GraphLab, the startup that became Turi, in 2013.

articles.title: Trump calls for Jensen Huang reinstatement as Nvidia CEO
articles.content: Following reports that ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is plotting a return to the company , President Donald Trump has voiced his own support for such a move, Bloomberg reports. However, according to new insight from CNBC , Nvidia's board of directors is not considering the move and is instead focused on its ongoing investigation into Huang's extramarital affairs and a national security investigation, likely into possible allegations of chip smuggling into China . Trump reportedly made his comments in support of Huang's return to reporters at the White House on Monday, ahead of his trip to Asia. "I would not mind that," he said. "A lot of people are asking Jensen; they think Jensen should go back. That certainly isn’t a bad idea.” While Trump noted Huang's financial situation, he said the CEO did not put national security at risk and did not know Megaspeed executive Alice Huang was suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset . Last week, the President said that Apple's former CEO Tim Cook was the only man to replace Huang in Nvidia's top job. Trump's comments also contrast sharply with those of Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who this week has called for Nvidia to replace Huang with an outsider, while giving the company 100 days to explain its dealings with China. As mentioned, Jensen Huang's purported return does not seem to be an option the board is seriously considering. A person familiar with the matter told CNBC that the board of directors is focused on investigating Huang's conduct and a national security investigation and is not discussing his return. A large petition has started circulating pertaining to Huang's reinstatement, with Elon Musk the most notable to sign . Musk had ventured so far as to say it would be an 'honor' to hire Huang , presumably to his Terafab project, following revelations of his exit. While rumblings of possible illicit chip smuggling into China have dogged Nvidia for well over a year, Huang's tenure as founder and CEO ended somewhat abruptly last week after a series of revelations spiraled to bring about his resignation. In the wake of reports that US officials were said to be concerned about his close relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, it later transpired that Huang had indeed had an affair with Ms. Huang, and that there were suspicions she was a Chinese intelligence asset. Since that news broke, it has further been revealed that Huang also had an inappropriate relationship with one of his direct reports, Nvidia's VP of health care, Kimberly Powell , and that the company covered up the fling. Perhaps more concerningly for Jensen Huang, it has been alleged that Ms. Huang and Megaspeed may have been involved in chip smuggling into China to the tune of more than $7 billion , with hundreds of thousands of H100 and H200 chips said to have found their way into the country at her behest, a factor analysts believe may be the true reason behind Huang's exit. For now, Nvidia's former CFO Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO, with one of her first orders of business the company's earnings call on November 17. The company's shares have tumbled sharply in the last week, perhaps understandably. Shares were down more than 4% on Monday, and more than 10% over the last five days, with the stock on course to lose nearly one-third of its value in the last six months.

articles.title: How MoEngage built agentic customer engagement on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
articles.content: This post was co-written with Ashwin Srinivasan, Nishan Das and Karthik Baile from MoEngage. A marketing or product team member planning a weekend flash sale often opens three tools before writing a single line of copy. First they open the analytics dashboard to see what worked last time, then the content library to find the right tone, and then the campaign builder to build the campaign itself. Repeat that across email, push, SMS, and WhatsApp, and much of a marketing team’s week goes to navigating tools instead of making decisions. The MoEngage Model Context Protocol (MCP) Connector gives an MCP-compatible assistant, such as Claude or ChatGPT, secure, tenant-scoped access to a brand’s segments, campaign history, and content library. This capability points to a broader shift in software platforms. Beyond a user interface for business users and an API for engineering teams, a third layer is emerging, where a user describes an outcome in plain language and an agent carries out the steps across the platform. For a customer engagement platform, that means a capability already exposed as an API can become a tool an agent calls, and a campaign that once moved across several tools can move through one conversation instead. MoEngage, the agentic customer engagement platform that more than 1,350 consumer brands use across channels including push, email, in-app, SMS, WhatsApp, and Rich Communication Services (RCS), set out to build this layer. MoEngage built Merlin AI, a set of artificial intelligence (AI) agents that work with live platform data. Marketing and product teams can now draft, analyze, and adjust campaigns from a single conversation, while agents decide what to send each customer. One customer, Glance, saw a 38% uplift in push notification click-through rates as a result. MoEngage treated this as an architecture problem. The question was how to give agents secure, tenant-scoped access to live data without rebuilding hundreds of existing APIs. In this post, we walk through how MoEngage solved it with Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, a platform to build, connect, and optimize AI agents at scale with any framework or model. The post covers the four agent modes in Merlin AI, how MoEngage exposed its existing APIs as MCP tools, and how the architecture keeps each tenant’s data isolated. It closes with the results MoEngage customers have seen and the pattern other software providers can reuse. Solution overview: Four agent modes in Merlin AI Merlin AI runs four kinds of agents. All four share the same foundation: foundation models in Amazon Bedrock for reasoning and generation, AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, for hosting, and MCP for standardized access to data. Across all four modes, Merlin AI uses Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Sonnet 5, and Claude Sonnet 5.5 on Amazon Bedrock for reasoning, tool-call planning, and content generation. For the full list of models, see Supported foundation models in Amazon Bedrock . Embedded agents in Merlin AI Studio Merlin AI Studio places purpose-built agents at the exact point in the workflow where marketing and product teams do that piece of work: Copywriter generates personalized push and transactional copy that stays consistent with the brand voice. Designer produces a marketing banner or image from a text description. Segment Assist turns a plain-language audience description into the correct set of attributes and filters. For example, a marketing or product team member can ask for users who abandoned a cart in the last 2 hours. Jinja Assist converts natural-language requests into working Jinja and Liquid markup for dynamic content. In-app Template Builder creates responsive, accessible HTML templates for in-app messages, including gamified formats, lead-capture pop-ups, and surveys. Flow Assist turns a high-level idea into a ready-to-deploy customer journey. Behind the scenes, a sequence of specialized steps interprets the request, proposes…

articles.title: Study: 403 U.S. hyperscale data centers rival Denmark’s emissions; Oregon ranked No. 2 in power use
articles.content: Data centers plugged into the grid in Quincy, Wash. (GeekWire Photo / Lisa Stiffler) A Harvard-led study estimates that electricity use at 403 U.S. hyperscale data centers was equal to roughly 25.7 million metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions — a volume roughly comparable to Denmark’s carbon footprint. The research examined some of the nation’s largest and most powerful data center facilities operating between May 2024 and April 2025. Together, those facilities accounted for an estimated 1.8% of total U.S. electricity consumption. “What we’re seeing is already striking, but it’s only a snapshot of a rapidly expanding industry,” Gianluca Guidi, the study’s lead author and a postdoctoral fellow in the Department of Biostatistics at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, said in a statement. Guidi noted that the data center boom has continued since the study period ended. “That means the electricity use and carbon footprint we’re reporting could already be substantially larger now in 2026.” Related Data center developers brace for new reality as election backlash sinks in The research, published in the journal Nature Sustainability and explored in an associated website , comes amid growing pushback and concerns about the facilities’ impacts on electric bills, water consumption, noise and carbon emissions. In the Pacific Northwest, government officials are enacting moratoriums and exploring legislation to regulate data center development. Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek in October directed a state agency to pause processing and issuing permits for new and expanding data centers until July 2027. In Washington, state Rep. Beth Doglio, D-Olympia, will propose data center rules in the legislative session that starts in January. Hyperscale sites handle massive computing workloads and data storage, supporting operations including large language model training and AI deployment. The researchers found that Oregon ranked second in electricity used by hyperscale data centers in the study, consuming about half as much as those in Virginia. Given Oregon’s access to clean hydropower, the state ranked sixth in carbon dioxide emissions attributed to the facilities’ electricity use. The publication highlighted data from the top 10 states for energy use, which does not include Washington. Nationwide, roughly 54% of the electricity attributed to the facilities came from fossil fuels, primarily natural gas and coal. The estimates were based on regional power generation mixes, not individual operators’ clean energy purchases. The study did not break out energy use by data center operator. Amazon, Microsoft and Google have the largest data center footprints worldwide and account for 57% of hyperscale data center capacity, according to Synergy Research Group . All three have aggressive carbon reduction targets. While their emissions have all increased in recent years, the companies say they remain committed to their goals. Microsoft and Amazon point to their support for new clean power projects and investments in low-carbon building materials for the facilities as positive steps towards reductions. “We continue to really be focused around carbon negativity by 2030,” Melanie Nakagawa, Microsoft’s chief sustainability officer, told GeekWire in July . Kara Hurst, Amazon’s chief sustainability officer, acknowledged that it will be difficult for the company to reach its target of net-zero emissions by 2040. “So that is a real challenge,” Hurst said in September , “and we’re here to meet the moment. I’m not saying that it’s going to be easy, and I’m not saying it’s going to be linear. But we’re going to put everything we have behind that.” At the same time, both tech giants are pursuing projects involving fossil fuel energy in Texas. Microsoft in June signed a 20-year deal to purchase power from a natural gas facility slated to come online in 2028. Amazon has agreed to become the anchor tenant of a massive planned data center campus with…

articles.title: SpaceX Catches Starship On the First Try
articles.content: Over the weekend, SpaceX successfully caught a Starship upper stage returning from orbit for the first time, demonstrating a key piece of its plan for a fully and rapidly reusable launch system. The achievement means SpaceX has now demonstrated tower catches of both Starship stages, though not yet on the same flight. "Many small fixes are needed to achieve immediate reusability (like an airplane)," noted SpaceX's Elon Musk. The Register reports: Flight 15 began well, with the 33 Raptor engines of the Super Heavy booster launching the stack from Pad 2 at Starbase, Texas. Hot staging followed, and the booster performed its directional flip maneuver. Thirty-two Raptor engines relit for the boostback burn, intended to return Super Heavy to the tower for another catch. The booster had managed the maneuver on flight tests 5, 7, and 8, but this time something went wrong. "The boostback burn ended early due to low fuel mass," SpaceX said. The booster automatically aborted its return to the tower and diverted offshore. It completed a landing burn, briefly hovering above the Gulf before its engines shut down and the flight termination system delivered an explosive finale. Starship reached orbit under the power of its six Raptor engines and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites. Unlike the previous flight's brief orbital stint, this mission lasted almost a day. Following a deorbit burn, Starship returned to the launch site 22 and a half hours after it left. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Dax Raad rebuilt his browser tool in Rust for $60. Then memory use fell 97%.
articles.content: OpenCode developer Dax Raad says he rebuilt the project’s browser automation tool in Rust for $60, replacing the parts of Playwright and Patchright it actually used and dramatically reducing its memory footprint. A 4.3 MB binary The figures he posted to X on Saturday are striking. The new Rust binary is just 4.3 MB, compared with 53 to 64 MB for the previous Node version. Memory use for each OpenCode Browse connector also fell from roughly 190 MB to 5.6 MB after a few calls, a reduction of about 97%. The new Rust binary is just 4.3 MB, compared with 53 to 64 MB for the previous Node version. The relay that wires AI coding agents to the browser shows a similar gap, with Raad’s comparison putting the Rust implementation at 6 MB idle, or 6.6 MB once it has served calls, against 353 MB for the old Node relay after six days of running. Replacing Playwright and Patchright OpenCode Browse connects AI coding agents to a developer’s existing browser through a Chromium extension and an MCP server . The previous Node implementation used Playwright for browser automation and Patchright to reduce detection, but Raad rebuilt the functionality Browse needed in Rust to cut runtime overhead. Raad rebuilt the functionality Browse needed in Rust to cut runtime overhead. The new Rust relay communicates with the Chromium extension over WebSockets and uses the Chrome DevTools Protocol to handle browser operations, agent sessions, recordings, and network captures. It also embeds QuickJS to execute agent-supplied JavaScript without requiring the previous Node runtime. Inside the pull request The merged pull request confirms that Raad replaced the Node-based CLI and relay while keeping the existing Chromium extension and using the Chrome DevTools Protocol for browser operations. The team ran two rounds of testing with about 10 regression agents against a real Chrome browser. Browse scored 85% on Stealth Bench v2, compared with 90.5% for Browser Use Cloud, although the pull request doesn’t include a score for the old Node version. Not everything made it into the rewrite; Raad dropped time zone and locale emulation along with the download tool, which Chrome blocks for extensions. The Rust version also retains a problem from the Node implementation where a busy-looping eval can’t be stopped through the extension. Browse still includes relay authentication, extension pairing and origin restrictions, and agents are limited to tabs they open themselves or that users explicitly share with them. The real $60 cost Raad says the rewrite “only cost $60” and confirmed in a reply on X that he used Claude Opus as his main coding model and DeepSeek as a subagent. The two models helped him replace the Playwright and Patchright functionality Browse needed, although the $60 figure doesn’t include the time he spent checking, testing, and fixing the code. The challenge with Rust rewrites is finding a smaller replacement that matches the original’s functionality without creating more maintenance work. the $60 figure doesn’t include the time he spent checking, testing, and fixing the code The memory savings are impressive, but Raad has also taken on responsibility for code that Playwright and Patchright previously maintained. His team will also have to deal with browser updates, authentication changes and security fixes that previously came through those libraries. That’s where AI-generated technical debt can become a problem, especially when code is cheap to produce but takes considerably more work to maintain. articles.title: Modernizing mainframe Assembler to Java using Amazon Bedrock and AWS Transform
articles.content: Imagine a batch job that has run every night for decades without failing, and the only person who understands its code is about to retire. We have seen this situation again and again while working with banking, insurance, and airline customers. Their Assembler programs still run critical business operations, but fewer people can read them each year. Rewriting them by hand takes years, risks breaking business rules nobody remembers writing, and still depends on the same experts who are leaving. Amazon Bedrock and AWS Transform change that equation. This post shows you a multi-stage transformation methodology using Amazon Bedrock , Kiro IDE (an AI-powered integrated development environment), and AWS Transform that can help reduce modernization time compared to manual approaches while maintaining business logic integrity through validation checkpoints. You will learn how to systematically extract business rules from Assembler code, convert them through an intermediate COBOL stage, and deploy modernized applications as Java Spring Boot services on AWS. Prerequisites Before starting the modernization process, make sure you have: Active AWS account with least-privilege AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) permissions for Amazon Bedrock, AWS Transform, and Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3). Access to Amazon Q Developer or Kiro for AI-assisted code analysis. Access to AWS Transform for COBOL to Java conversion. Access to Amazon Bedrock with appropriate foundation models (FMs). An Amazon S3 bucket configured for source code and artifact storage, with encryption and Block Public Access enabled. Knowledge of the target business domain and application functionality. Availability of business and technical subject matter experts (SMEs) for validation sessions. Source Assembler code inventory with available documentation. Test data sets with expected outputs for functional equivalence testing. Solution overview You can transform legacy mainframe Assembler applications tightly bounded with COBOL into Java Spring Boot applications built for the AWS cloud through a systematic five-phase approach. This multi-stage methodology, converting Assembler to COBOL as an intermediate step before Java transformation, reduces risk and preserves business logic with greater reliability than direct Assembler-to-Java conversion. The intermediate COBOL stage provides a structured, human-readable format that subject matter experts (SMEs) can validate before final transformation. This makes sure that business rules remain intact throughout the modernization journey. The following sections describe both the current mainframe architecture and the target cloud-focused state. Current state Your current architecture represents a traditional mainframe environment where Assembler programs execute batch processes, connected with COBOL, interact with databases, and process files. At its core, JCL (Job Control Language) jobs trigger Assembler program execution at scheduled intervals. These programs read input from VSAM (Virtual Storage Access Method) and sequential files and perform operations against IBM Db2 for z/OS. Your business logic executes using low-level register operations (direct CPU register manipulation) and memory management. Output is written back to files or database tables, and job completion status is reported through JCL return codes. All of this runs on IBM z/OS mainframe infrastructure. Figure 1: Mainframe Assembler architecture Target state The modernization solution helps you transform legacy mainframe Assembler applications into Java applications built for the AWS cloud through a multi-phase, AI-powered workflow. The architecture uses Amazon Bedrock and Kiro IDE for AI-assisted code analysis and business rule extraction, and AWS Transform for automated COBOL-to-Java conversion. If COBOL source code is already available, you follow the conventional approach and provide it directly to AWS Transform for conversion to Java Spring Boot…

articles.title: Ahead of its IPO filing, Anthropic pledges to prioritize humanity’s benefit. Here’s how
articles.content: When Anthropic goes public on Wall Street, the new pressure to deliver profits will test a commitment it has made since its founding: to prioritize humanity’s benefit as it develops artificial intelligence . The San Francisco startup, which plans an initial public offering this month, has sketched out a governance structure that it says will protect the company’s broader mission against the pull of financial interests. But the mechanisms it describes give the company wide leeway to decide how to measure whether it’s benefiting society, experts say. Like its rival OpenAI , Anthropic is a public benefit corporation, a legal designation used by companies that pledge to balance shareholder interests with the public good. How that will play out for companies worth potentially trillions of dollars is uncharted territory. “I think then the real test emerges if and when the question of public benefit becomes costly” — or when the public benefit comes into conflict with making a profit, said Sarah Kreps, a professor and director of Cornell University’s Tech Policy Institute. In its regulatory filings, Anthropic pledges to pursue long-term benefits of humanity through the responsible development of advanced AI . “We strive to help bring humanity safely into an era where transformative AI exerts tremendous and potentially decisive influence over a broad range of human undertakings,” the company said. Anthropic also has pledged at least 5% of its stock to a “public benefit” fund and its founders have committed to donate 80% of their wealth. A pledge to do good is baked into corporate structure Other tech companies have pledged to do good including Google, which prominently featured its then-motto, “Don’t Be Evil,” in its investor prospectus when it went public in 2004. But the words were not legally binding, and critics have accused the tech giant of leaving them behind. Elon Musk’s takeover of Twitter in 2021 shows how the conflict between profit and public good might play out in real life, said Stavros Gadinis, a law professor at UC Berkeley School of Law. “Let’s say that Twitter’s directors felt that Elon was the wrong guy to police the public square because they didn’t trust him, they didn’t like him, they didn’t think he’d be fair, whatever it was,” Gadinis said. “But he made them an offer that was so high compared to what their advisors told them the company was really worth that it would be against their fiduciary duties to not sell to Elon. This is the situation that the public benefit charter is trying to avoid.” Had Twitter been a public benefit corporation, it could have been required to consider factors beyond maximizing shareholder value when selling the company. There aren’t many public benefit corporations whose shares are publicly traded and they are all much smaller than Anthropic and OpenAI. They include the eyewear company Warby Parker, the insurance company Lemonade and software developer Veeva Systems, which had a conventional corporate structure when it went public in 2013 and converted to a public benefit corporation in 2021. Anthropic’s idealistic ambitions for how it develops AI could run up against competitive pressure, such as from China, Kreps said. Anthropic and OpenAI’s models have gone from answering almost any question, even if it was dangerous, to becoming much more circumspect. But as they face more competition, including from open-source Chinese models that likely will tell you whatever you want, she said, “will they start to rethink some of those guardrails? And what happens then?” The setup generally is not preferred by shareholders because it gives more power to the company’s board than it does to shareholders. Whatever a company decides as its public benefit mission, it will likely be much more difficult to measure than…
